meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session August 3, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on August 3, 2026, featuring extensive public comments and board discussions regarding a proposed data center moratorium, NCACC legislative priorities for the upcoming biennium, and school/community funding needs. Formal actions included appointing NCACC voting delegates (passing 4-0 after suspending rules) and approving a 15.7% salary increase for the DSS director following closed session (passing unanimously).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order & Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the August 3, 2026 work session with Chair Lee reading the public charge and Commissioner Burton reading the land acknowledgement recognizing indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Housing & Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community members spoke during citizen comments regarding affordable housing initiatives, specifically introducing Forest Grove Homes, an inclusive housing community for adults with developmental disabilities and veterans.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Data Center Moratorium
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Numerous speakers from local advocacy groups, RTP representatives, and residents addressed the board regarding a proposed data center moratorium, discussing water/electricity consumption, PFAS, noise, and exemptions.

agenda_items.title: Data Center Moratorium Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members discussed the draft data center moratorium, timelines, exemption criteria, square footage thresholds, and alignment with the city's moratorium language.

agenda_items.title: Transit & Transportation Study Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presentation and discussion on transit initiatives, studies, and regional transportation planning.

agenda_items.title: 2027 Legislative Goals Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the upcoming 2027 legislative goals process, including proposals from Veteran Services, Engineering (reclaimed water use, EV charging station user fees), and commissioner priorities.

agenda_items.title: NCACC Voting Delegate Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to suspend rules and appoint Commissioner Burton as the NCACC voting delegate and Commissioner Jacobs as the alternate.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session & DSS Director Salary Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved into closed session and subsequently approved a 15.7% salary increase for the DSS Director to align with market fairness.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Closed session passed 4-0; DSS salary passed unanimously)

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for NCACC Voting Delegate Appointment
votes.discussion_detail: During the Durham Board of County Commissioners work session on August 3, 2026, the board addressed final legislative goals, including a proposal from engineering to authorize counties to charge user fees for public electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Tobin Freed, sustainability manager, noted that counties were previously overlooked when a law was passed allowing cities to charge for EV charging stations, and legislative corrections are currently being pursued to allow counties to do the same to recoup costs and manage stations. Following these discussions, the board considered the appointment of the voting delegate and alternate for the NCACC conference, requiring a procedural motion to suspend the rules. Commissioner Valentine moved to suspend the rules, which was seconded by Commissioner Jacobs and passed unanimously by a 4-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Appoint NCACC Voting Delegate and Alternate
votes.discussion_detail: Following the suspension of the rules during the August 3, 2026 work session, the board moved to appoint its voting delegate and alternate for the upcoming NCACC conference. Commissioner Valentine moved that Commissioner Burton serve as the delegate and Commissioner Jacobs serve as the alternate, which was seconded by Commissioner Burton. The motion passed unanimously with a 4-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Move into Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: As the final order of business during the August 3, 2026 work session, the board transitioned into a closed session pursuant to General Statute 143-318.116. Commissioner Burton moved to enter closed session, seconded by Commissioner Valentine. The motion was approved unanimously in a 4-0 vote.

votes.item_title: DSS Director Salary Increase
votes.discussion_detail: Following a closed session during the August 3, 2026 meeting, the board reconvened and considered a proposal presented by Dr. Lee to increase the salary of the DSS director by 15.7% to align with market fairness and rates. A proper motion was made and seconded, and following an opportunity for discussion, the board voted unanimously to approve the salary increase. With no further business on the agenda, the meeting was adjourned.

disagreements.issue: Data Center Moratorium Language and Exemptions
disagreements.summary: Discussion on whether the county should adopt moratorium language matching the city's version or keep its own distinct draft with specific enterprise/square-footage exemptions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support aligning the county's moratorium language closely with the city's version.
side_a_arguments: Aligning with the city's moratorium language and definitions makes joint city-county planning staff work easier and avoids confusion.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support county-specific draft language and further review of exemptions and square footage thresholds.
side_b_arguments: County land uses in RTP and Treyburn differ from city land uses, requiring county-specific wording; exemptions or square footage thresholds need careful review to protect smaller business server needs without creating loopholes.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken on the moratorium text; consensus was reached to schedule a public hearing for August 24, 2026, while commissioners review draft language and exemptions.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: Work Session Consent Review: Request for Sheriff's Training Facility Status Update (26-0387) & Capital Reallocation Clarification (26-0249)
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: Manager Hager presented consent items including a $933,464.49 capital reallocation to Sheriff's Office CAD/RMS software (26-0249) and $134,600 in furnishings for the Sheriff's Training Facility (26-0387), agreeing to coordinate with the Sheriff for a future work-session status update on the training center.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs asked Manager Hager for quick clarification on item 26-0249 to confirm for the public that the Sheriff's CAD/RMS funding was merely reallocating previously approved capital dollars from completed projects, accepting Hager's confirmation.
member_positions.key_quote: So this we had already approved this capital purchase, we're just reallocating previous capital funding from other projects to go towards it.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Valentine interrupted Manager Hager's presentation of item 26-0387 (training facility furnishings) to press for a formal work-session update on the overall status of the Sheriff's Training Center, prompting Hager to commit to scheduling it with the Sheriff.
member_positions.key_quote: County manager, before we proceed, I just have a question sort of tangential to 26-0387: are we going to be provided with an update regarding the status of the training center?

bocc_manager_events.event_title: Proposed Data Center Moratorium & Administration's 80,000-100,000 Sq Ft Carveout (26-0404)
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: Deputy County Manager Maurice Jones and planning staff presented the administration's draft nine-month data center moratorium featuring an 80,000 to 100,000 square-foot exemption for smaller enterprise data centers and broader economic-development exemptions than the City of Durham's moratorium.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Burton thanked DCM Jones and planning staff for defining data center types and asked for energy and water usage data on the county's 14 existing facilities, but pushed back against including carveouts in the moratorium itself, urging staff to reserve exemptions for the permanent ordinance.
member_positions.key_quote: I personally would like to just say let's not put any loopholes, leave that for the ordinance.

member_positions.stance_summary: Vice Chair Allam opposed the administration's proposed 80,000-100,000 sq ft carveout and county-specific exceptions, arguing that carveouts undermine the nine-month study period and pressing staff on why the county should not adopt the exact same broad moratorium passed by the City.
member_positions.key_quote: My concern is around having carveouts that won't allow us to properly use these nine months to define what a data center is, what the different levels are for Durham County and our needs.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Valentine expressed discomfort with the administration's proposed square-footage exemption, stating he favored removing that loophole until staff provides stronger data, while asking staff to assess impacts on RTP and Treyburn before the August 24 public hearing.
member_positions.key_quote: I'm not comfortable presently with making a determination regarding that, so to the extent that that would be one of the loopholes that are under consideration, I would be in favor of removing that.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs praised the County Attorney, Deputy County Manager, and planning staff for drafting legally clear moratorium language tailored to RTP and Treyburn rather than copying the City's version, while requesting follow-up verification from RTP on whether any RTP 3.0 projects would be harmed.
member_positions.key_quote: I just want to pull out our staff because I think that our moratorium language is very clear, the way it's laid out, and I want to thank the staff, our attorney for your work on that.

member_positions.stance_summary: Chair Lee backed the administration's proposed square-footage demarcation line (supporting 100,000 sq ft), arguing that a blanket moratorium without a threshold could sweep up small businesses, startups, and hospital/school server rooms, while stating he supports banning hyperscale AI data centers.
member_positions.key_quote: Well, I would support a demarcation line of 100,000 square feet simply because a blanket moratorium can sweep up server rooms.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Refresh: Prioritization Rubric, Tax Cap Risks, School Bonds & Stadium Study Transparency
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: Manager Hager introduced the 10-year CIP refresh ($1.5B-$2B) emphasizing shovel readiness, escalating construction/tariff costs, and a projected 4-cent tax increase over three years for existing debt, warning that a state property-tax cap would jeopardize operating programs and agreeing to bring back a CIP prioritization rubric.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Burton thanked staff for flagging DPS's $2 billion in identified capital needs and recognizing tough choices ahead, and later asked staff to confirm for community clarity that the 808 East Pettigrew study covered the former John Avery Boys and Girls Club property.
member_positions.key_quote: I wanted to thank you for this presentation about the schools and where that fit in, $2 billion and yeah, tough decisions are going to have to be made.

member_positions.stance_summary: Vice Chair Allam pressed Manager Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane on the timeline for a 2028 school bond referendum, cost-sharing status for the Museum of Durham History, and whether the county could pursue dedicated local taxes or standalone solar bonds for county and DPS facilities.
member_positions.key_quote: Wondering when are we having our next conversation about school bonds?

member_positions.stance_summary: After initially probing the 4-cent CIP tax projection, Commissioner Valentine challenged Manager Hager and staff over transparency when Commissioner Jacobs mentioned an ongoing stadium study that had been omitted from the CIP presentation, pressing Hager on whether it tied to NCCU athletics and county liability.
member_positions.key_quote: Back to managing our CIP, I heard moments ago about stadium study, I didn't know anything about it, it's not mentioned in the presentation.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs pressed Manager Hager on how a proposed state constitutional property tax cap could derail the existing CIP debt schedule, and urged Manager Hager and staff to create a formal CIP decision-making rubric separating legally mandated services from strategic priorities and consolidation opportunities.
member_positions.key_quote: It seems like in the future we're going to need some type of decision-making rubric, like what projects are related to essential mandated services, things that we absolutely have to do, versus what are the things that we really value but they're not essential.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session July 13, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners convened for their regular session on July 13, 2026, featuring a ceremonial resolution honoring civil rights icon Dr. Virginia Williams, public comments on child welfare, and discussions on economic development. The board unanimously approved an economic development performance agreement with AbbVie (not to exceed $15,450,000) after a motion to reconsider and add the specific funding cap, along with various board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the regular session, reciting the public charge and land acknowledgement covering indigenous peoples of the region. Staff and commissioners reviewed meeting procedures and decorum.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the agenda as presented with unanimous consent.

agenda_items.title: Board and Staff Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace read published announcements including solid waste convenience site closures, the launch of PayDECOnline for property tax payments, Sheriff Burkehead's upcoming speaking engagement at NALEO, school supply collections, and the InTouch with Durham County episode. Commissioners also discussed upcoming items such as the data centers moratorium and treatment court discussions.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (June 22, 2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from the June 22, 2026 regular session meeting and approved them unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Dr. Virginia Williams
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a ceremonial resolution honoring civil rights icon Dr. Virginia Williams, the last surviving member of the Royal Ice Cream 7, recognizing her historic 1957 sit-in protest and upcoming award at the International Civil Rights Center and Museum. Remarks were delivered by Commissioner Valentine, Pastor Dr. Abdu Knox, and Dr. Williams herself.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board announced various appointments to county boards and commissions, including the ABC Board, DSS Board, Durham Convention Center Authority, Women's Commission, and Library Board of Trustees.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens spoke during public comments regarding child welfare statistics, Department of Social Services (DSS) foster care transparency, judicial overreach, and community advocacy. Speakers raised concerns about children in custody, missing youth, and accountability.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Performance Agreement with AbbVie
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an economic development performance agreement with AbbVie for a major life sciences project involving a $1.4 billion investment and 734 new jobs, backed by an incentive award not to exceed $15,450,000. Commissioners engaged in extensive discussion regarding workforce pipelines, partnerships with Durham Tech and NCCU, property tax revenue projections, and local community benefits.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (with reconsideration to include not-to-exceed cap)

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: The Board of County Commissioners opened their regular session meeting on July 13, 2026, with the public charge, a land acknowledgement led by Commissioner Jacobs, and the pledge led by Commissioner Valentine. Following these introductory items and announcements regarding solid waste site closures and new digital tax payment platforms, the board reviewed the meeting agenda. A motion to approve the agenda as presented was made, seconded, and passed unanimously with no opposition.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (June 22, 2026)
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the approval of the minutes from the regular session meeting held on June 22, 2026. After confirming that the members had reviewed the record, a motion to approve the minutes was duly made and seconded. The motion passed unanimously without further discussion or opposition.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Performance Agreement with AbbVie (Not to exceed $15,450,000)
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered an economic development performance agreement with AbbVie. Commissioners expressed enthusiasm for the transformational project, emphasizing workforce diversity, local small business contracting opportunities, and anticipated property tax revenues to support county services. Following initial discussion, a motion was made and seconded to authorize the county manager to negotiate and execute the agreement. After the initial vote, members noted that the specific 'not to exceed' amount of $15,450,000 should be explicitly included in the motion language. A motion to reconsider the previous vote was properly made and seconded, followed by a motion to approve the performance agreement with the explicit cap of $15,450,000, which passed unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session June 22nd, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on June 22, 2026, chaired by Dr. Mike Lee. The board recognized incoming and retiring officials including Fire Marshal Tyler Fitts and Soil & Water Director Eddie Culverson, celebrated the 50th anniversary of the General Services Department, and received proclamations. The board also filled numerous board and commission vacancies, approved the consent agenda with discussion on opioid settlement funds, and unanimously approved zoning and UDO text amendment items following public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered and approved excused absences for Commissioner Jacobs and reviewed the meeting agenda as presented. The agenda adjustments passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the minutes from the June 1, 2026 work session and June 8, 2026 regular session meeting. The motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Tyler Fitts as Chief Fire Marshal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Mark Lockhart introduced Tyler Fitts as Durham County's new chief fire marshal in the Office of Emergency Services. Fitts, who has served nearly two decades in fire service and 8 years with Durham County, expressed his gratitude and commitment to public safety. Commissioners commended Fitts on his internal promotion and highlighted the critical importance of fire marshal inspections in local schools.

agenda_items.title: Announcements & Tributes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace presented announcements regarding free summer meals for youth under 18, a community summit on saving lives addressing violence reduction, a new fatherhood program by DSS, a Durham County Library donut crawl, and the latest episode of 'In Touch with Durham County'. Commissioners also paid personal tributes to the late local activist and minister Paul Scott, Orange County Commissioner Jamesetta Bedford, and discussed men's health and prostate cancer awareness.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Eddie Culverson, Soil and Water Director
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Dayne Branson and Soil and Water Board Vice Chair recognized Eddie Culverson, Soil and Water Director, for his 42 years of service (38 with Durham County) upon his retirement effective July 1st. Speakers lauded his leadership in making Durham County's soil and water district one of the top-performing in the state. Culverson shared reflections on his career and expressed appreciation for county leadership and staff.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Celebrating 50 Years of General Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Valentine read a resolution celebrating 50 years of service by the Department of General Services. General Services Director Moturo Key Umbral Arrow and staff members highlighted the department's operations managing over 2 million square feet and 70 buildings. Commissioners praised the department's responsiveness and dedication in maintaining county facilities.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations & Acknowledgments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board acknowledged several proclamations, including World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, Durham Refugee Day, and Summer Learning Week. Representatives from DSS Adult Services and refugee support spoke on the importance of these observances.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Pull Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the consent agenda, pulling three items (26-0334, 26-0336, 26-0337) for public comment. Commissioner Valentine raised unreadiness regarding opioid settlement fund allocation processes (item 26-0321), calling for a comprehensive review of resource distribution between county and community programs. The remainder of the consent agenda was approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change - Rupert Landscape (Z2500002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented rezoning application Z2500002 for Rupert Landscape, proposing to rezone 0.4 acres at 3513 Nance Avenue from Residential Suburban 20 (RS-20) to Industrial Light (IL) with a textual development plan to permit parking for an adjacent landscaping business. The Planning Commission voted 12-0 for a positive recommendation, and staff recommended a place type change to Suburban Commercial. The applicant noted strong community support and consistency with surrounding land uses.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously (two motions: ordinance and consistency statement)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment on Development Moratoriums (TC-2600002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented text amendment TC-2600002, a staff-initiated proposal to remove barriers and redundant standards in the UDO governing development moratoriums, aligning local rules with NC General Statute 160D-107. Thirteen public speakers provided comments, primarily supporting the text amendment as a tool to enable future moratoriums on data centers and protect local water resources. Commissioners praised staff and the County Attorney for proactive legal review.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously (two motions: ordinance and consistency statement)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board filled numerous vacancies across advisory boards and commissions, including the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, Board of Adjustment, Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, Open Space and Trails Commission, Planning Commission, Sports Commission, DTCC Board of Trustees, Environmental Affairs Board, Homeless Services Advisory Committee, and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council. Appointments were made unanimously, while the Women's Commission appointment was deferred due to a tie.

agenda_items.title: Items Pulled from Consent Agenda & Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comment was heard on three pulled consent items: item 26-0334 (service contract with Recovery Innovations Inc. for after-hours/telehealth mental health services at the detention center), item 26-0336 (service contract with Just Clean House Inc. for transitional living for Justice Services), and item 26-0337 (service contract with Psychiatric Services and Consultation for environmental health/detention mental health). Speaker Antoinette Hobbs expressed support for detention mental health services while criticizing broader community mental health allocation. All three pulled items were subsequently approved unanimously.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Commissioner Jacobs
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Valentine moved to excuse the absence of Commissioner Jacobs from the meeting. The motion was seconded and put to a voice vote, passing unanimously with all participating commissioners voting aye.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Following review of agenda adjustments, a motion was made and seconded to approve the meeting agenda as presented. The motion received unanimous support during voice voting.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Minutes (June 1 and June 8, 2026)
votes.discussion_detail: A motion was offered and seconded to approve the minutes of the June 1, 2026 work session and June 8, 2026 regular session. The chair called for discussion, and hearing none, called the vote, which passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approval of Consent Agenda (minus pulled items)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Valentine discussed unreadiness regarding the opioid settlement fund annual ordinance, calling for policy guidance and review of allocations. Following confirmation from staff that a review framework is planned for the fall, a motion was made and seconded to approve the consent agenda minus the three items pulled for public comment. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Rupert Landscape Rezoning Ordinance (Z2500002)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing on rezoning application Z2500002 for Rupert Landscape (changing 0.4 acres from RS-20 to Industrial Light with a textual development plan), a motion was made and seconded to adopt the ordinance amending the UDO. Commissioners noted unanimous planning commission recommendation and consistency with adjacent land use. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Rupert Landscape Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: As required by NC General Statute 160D-605, a motion was introduced and seconded to adopt the consistency statement for the Rupert Landscape rezoning case. The motion was debated briefly, put to a vote, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment on Moratoriums Ordinance (TC-2600002)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing on UDO text amendment TC-2600002 regarding development moratoriums, where 13 public speakers testified, a motion was offered and seconded to adopt the ordinance amending UDO Article 3. Commissioners expressed strong support for removing bureaucratic barriers to moratorium enactment. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment Consistency Statement (TC-2600002)

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session June 8th, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: In the second segment of the June 8, 2026 Durham Board of County Commissioners regular session, the board concluded ceremonial recognitions for Richard "Ricky" Christopher Dorsey, National Pride Month, Women Veterans Day, Gun Violence Awareness Month, and National Reunification Month, marked by pointed community criticism over Pride funding cuts and DSS child removal practices. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda 5-0 before holding public comment and extensive deliberations on the FY 2026-2027 budget ordinance. Commissioners debated whether to raise the property tax rate—by a quarter-cent, half-cent, or two cents—to address Durham Public Schools classified staff pay compression against competing county pressures including $3 million in absorbed federal DSS cuts, rising SNAP/Medicaid administrative mandates, and protecting the county's AAA bond rating; the video recording ended during Commissioner Stephen Valentine's remarks prior to a final budget vote.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring the Life, Service, and Sacrifice of Richard "Ricky" Christopher Dorsey (Conclusion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners thanked the Dorsey family for Ricky Dorsey's volunteer fire service starting at age 18 and his ultimate sacrifice during Hurricane Fran. Speakers noted the resolution supports ongoing efforts with NCDOT and the Durham legislative delegation to name the highway over the Little River Reservoir in his honor.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National Pride Month 2026
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nida Allam read the proclamation declaring June 2026 as National Pride Month in Durham County, citing the 1969 Stonewall Riots, the 1981 Our Day Out march in Durham, the 2026 theme "Always Forward, Never Straight, Preserving History, Coming Home," and the County Non-Discrimination Ordinance. LGBTQ Center of Durham leaders Jesse Huddleston and Rey Dooley urged commissioners to move beyond symbolic proclamations and take responsibility for repairing harm, referencing a 1986 library Pride display incident. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Stephen Valentine, Nida Allam, and Michelle Burton affirmed solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community and highlighted Pride Month events.

agenda_items.title: Resolution for Women Veterans Day 2026
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee noted that board procedures allow public comment only on consent and regular agenda items, though he made an executive decision to grant one minute per signed-up speaker on item 26-0306. Navy veteran and Durham County Veteran Service Officer Hayleen Windoly Rodriguez spoke on women's 250 years of military contributions and invited the public to the second annual Women's Veterans Recognition Day event on June 12. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Stephen Valentine commended Rodriguez and her team.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for Gun Violence Awareness Month 2026
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Crystal Harris, Director of Community Intervention and Support Services, accepted the proclamation recognizing June 2026 as Gun Violence Awareness Month and underscored collective responsibility for violence prevention. In response to Vice Chair Nida Allam, Harris outlined county investments including Project Build—recently expanded to youth ages 10-13 with 9-to-12-month aftercare—and Justice Services programs, while Commissioner Stephen Valentine emphasized community-wide partnership.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National Reunification Month 2026
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Four signed-up speakers (Walia Burns, Antoinette Halls, Amanda Wallace of Operation Stop CPS, and Sharaka Pettiford) criticized Durham County DSS during one-minute remarks, arguing the proclamation was hypocritical given foster care stays averaging over 677 days and demanding at least 1% of the county budget for family reunification and preservation. DSS Director Clapp thanked staff for their daily reunification work and noted Fatherhood Awareness Month. Audience member Amanda Wallace interrupted Director Clapp and, after repeated warnings from Chair Dr. Mike Lee, was removed from the chambers.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presented the consent agenda items moved forward from the board's work session and asked if any commissioner had comments or questions. Hearing none, the board voted unanimously by voice vote to approve the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Budget Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Four public commenters addressed the budget: Jack Turnwald and Laura Phoenix urged the board to apologize and restore Pride funding, library programming, and the eliminated LGBTQ committee, while DPS physical therapists Heidi Jo Hetland and Christie Clapp warned that two years without raises and severe classified staff attrition (leaving the PT department 55% staffed) risk federal IEP compliance failures. Budget Director Keith Lane and County Manager Hager described extreme fiscal constraints—over $40 million in requests above revenue, 2% cuts across most county departments, a 2% staff pay adjustment, and a projected $12 million FY 2027-28 gap. Commissioners debated potential property tax rate adjustments to support DPS classified staff versus protecting taxpayers and absorbing federal SNAP/Medicaid/DSS cuts; the recording ended at 01:11:11 during Commissioner Stephen Valentine's remarks before any vote occurred.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deliberated / Recording ended prior to vote

votes.item_title: Adoption of the Consent Agenda (items moved from Work Session)
votes.notes: Consent agenda items were moved forward from the prior work session; no items were pulled for separate discussion.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the ceremonial proclamations and the removal of an interrupting audience member, Chair Dr. Mike Lee introduced the consent agenda consisting of items forwarded from the board's work session. He invited comments or questions from commissioners before calling for a motion. A motion to approve the consent agenda was made and seconded without further debate. The board adopted the consent agenda unanimously by a 5-0 voice vote with all five commissioners present.

disagreements.issue: FY 2026-2027 Property Tax Rate, Durham Public Schools Classified Staff Funding, and County Fiscal Reserves
disagreements.summary: Commissioners and county leadership differed on whether to raise the property tax rate above the budget constraints—and by how much—to fund wage parity and raises for Durham Public Schools classified staff, versus holding down property taxes amid reassessment pressures, rising DPS debt service, and looming federal cuts to SNAP, Medicaid, and child welfare.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support a targeted property tax increase (such as a quarter-cent or half-cent) to close funding gaps for DPS classified staff and employee pay parity before potential state restrictions limit county taxing authority.
side_a_arguments: State legislation could restrict local governments' revenue-raising power next year, making FY 2026-27 a critical window to establish an equal minimum wage for DPS and county staff (Vice Chair Nida Allam).

A half-cent tax increase equates to $20 per year on a $400,000 home, and DPS classified staff—who have gone two years without raises and are losing physical therapists and support personnel—need relief (Vice Chair Nida Allam; public testimony from Heidi Jo Hetland and Christie Clapp).
Willing to support up to a quarter-cent tax increase specifically to fund needed raises for school staff while acknowledging resident tax fatigue (Commissioner Michelle Burton).
disagreements.side_b_position: Exercise caution against raising property tax rates further due to taxpayer burden from recent reassessments, upcoming DPS debt service, and the need to preserve fiscal stability and the AAA bond rating to absorb severe federal social services cuts.
side_b_arguments: Durham County already had to absorb $3 million in federal social services cuts, faces a 10% drop in SNAP participation, new 6-month SNAP/Medicaid eligibility reviews, 24-hour child welfare investigation mandates, and DSS staff attrition costing $150/day for temporary workers (Commissioner Wendy Jacobs).
Recurring tax increases lock in ongoing baseline expenses and risk Durham County's AAA bond rating, which is vital for affordable school construction borrowing (Commissioner Wendy Jacobs).

Residents have experienced steep property tax bills after reassessment, and the county faces strong multi-year fiscal headwinds alongside higher DPS debt service payments (County Manager Hager, echoed cautiously by Commissioner Stephen Valentine weighing the proposed 2-cent hike against low sales/occupancy tax revenue).
disagreements.resolution: Unresolved within this recording; the video ended at 01:11:11 during Commissioner Stephen Valentine's remarks prior to a motion or vote on the budget ordinance.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session June 1st, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on June 1st, 2026, featuring detailed discussions on the final recommended FY 2027 Annual Transit Work Program and potential regulatory policies regarding data centers. Commissioners reviewed transit funding priorities, service delays, and Go Triangle regional requests, while also evaluating staff research and a potential moratorium on hyperscale data centers. Additionally, the board convened in closed session to consult with legal counsel pursuant to attorney-client privilege.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Final Recommended FY 2027 Annual Transit Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff and Go Triangle representatives presented the final recommended FY 2027 Annual Transit Work Program, detailing funding allocations, slower sales tax growth, and operating budget reductions resulting from city-requested service delays. Go Triangle deputy CEO Katherine Eggleston provided comments advocating for immediate cost-neutral service adjustments for Route 800 and the Durham-Raleigh Express (DRX), while commissioners raised concerns about long-term financial sustainability, capital maintenance funding gaps, and the city's operating deficit.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational presentation and discussion only; no formal vote was taken during the work session, with formal action scheduled for the upcoming regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Future Data Center Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners discussed potential zoning regulations, land-use definitions, and a possible 12-month moratorium targeting hyperscale and large-scale data centers. The conversation explored infrastructure impacts such as water and power consumption, noise regulations, and distinctions between commercial/educational data centers and massive hyperscale facilities. Commissioners directed staff to continue researching appropriate regulatory language and exemptions for smaller business and institutional data centers.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Discussion item only; no formal vote was taken.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session - Attorney-Client Privilege Consultation

disagreements.issue: Whether to immediately incorporate Go Triangle's cost-neutral service adjustments (Route 800 reliability and DRX frequency) into the FY 2027 work program or defer them to a future amendment cycle, weighed against county concerns over financial sustainability, slowing sales tax growth, and capital funding shortfalls.
disagreements.summary: Debate between commissioners and Go Triangle representatives over incorporating regional transit service adjustments into the FY 2027 work program versus deferring them to an amendment cycle.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adhere to the staff working group's recommended work program and handle partner additions via future amendments due to financial and timing constraints.
side_a_arguments: Express concern over slowing sales tax revenue growth and significant capital funding gaps for bus maintenance facilities.
Caution against last-minute additions without thorough vetting, citing the city's ongoing transit fund operating deficit.
Prefer adhering to the staff working group's initial recommended draft or addressing late partner requests through a planned future amendment cycle.
disagreements.side_b_position: Immediately incorporate the cost-neutral regional service adjustments into the FY 2027 work program to address critical rider reliability needs.
side_b_arguments: Highlight urgent, documented rider needs and severe reliability issues on Route 800 (operating at 77% on-time performance).
Note that the proposed adjustments are cost-neutral, require no county tax increases, and are supported by the Go Triangle Board.
Emphasize the importance of resolving regional connectivity and reliability gaps immediately rather than risking prolonged procedural delays.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote or resolution was reached during the work session; the work program was presented as recommended by the staff working group for future consideration, while commissioners discussed the possibility of sending a clarifying letter to the city regarding one-time funding limits.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session June 1st, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 1, 2026 work session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened with the public charge and land acknowledgement before voting unanimously by voice vote (5-0) to enter a closed session under N.C.G.S. 132-1.7(a)(3) and 143-318.11(a)(1) regarding sensitive public security information, returning with no action taken and recessing for the Juneteenth flag-raising ceremony. After reconvening in open session, two public commenters urged the board to audit the Department of Social Services (DSS) and reallocate 1% of the social services budget toward family reunification and preservation rather than Family Treatment Court. County Manager Claudia Hager then presented seven consent agenda items—including a $16,999 Duke Energy Share the Light budget amendment, a $148,200 elevator maintenance contract, a $750,000 county contribution to Triangle Land Conservancy for 145 acres of farmland, and an OverDrive digital content contract—all of which were forwarded without vote to the regular session. Finally, the board began reviewing a time-sensitive request to suspend the rules for Budget Ordinance Amendment 26-BCC-086 ($1,379,000 from general fund balance for a sole-bidder detention center facility management contract with TKC Management Services), with the video ending mid-discussion prior to any vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the June 1, 2026 work session to order and read the public charge, and Vice Chair Nida Allam (transcribed as 'Vice Chair Lam') delivered the land acknowledgement. The board then moved, seconded, and voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session to prevent the disclosure of sensitive public security information under N.C.G.S. 132-1.7(a)(3) and pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (Voice vote to enter closed session; no action taken in closed session)

agenda_items.title: Return from Closed Session, Juneteenth Recess, and Reconvening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session at 02:18:37, Chair Dr. Mike Lee announced that no action had been taken and recessed the meeting so commissioners could attend the Juneteenth flag-raising ceremony and lunch. The board reconvened in open session at 03:53:14 to continue the regular work session agenda.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In-person speaker Antoninath Halles criticized board actions toward working-class and marginalized residents, urged an audit of the Department of Social Services (DSS), and called for 1% of the budget to support Child Protective Services family reunification and development alongside drug court. Online speaker Amanda Wallace (founder of Operation Stop CPS, transcribed as 'Operations.CPS') noted that Leslie Say-Drew (transcribed as 'Leslie, say, Drew') was in the virtual waiting room trying to speak, disputed prior work-session figures cited by Commissioner Stephen Valentine, and urged reallocating 1% of the social services budget (~$1 million split between family reunification and preservation) rather than funding Family Treatment Court.

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent Agenda Items (26-0261, 26-0263, 26-0264, 26-0266, 26-0283, 26-0284, 26-0298)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager presented seven consent items for review: Keep Durham Beautiful's 2025 annual report (26-0261), Budget Ordinance Amendment 26-BCC-084 recognizing $16,999 in Duke Energy Share the Light funds for DSS (26-0263), the FY 2026-27 Home and Community Care Block Grant county funding plan (26-0264), a $148,200 Southern Elevator Company contract (26-0266), a lease with Bull City Slabs LLC at Shops of Hope Valley (26-0283), a $750,000 contribution for Triangle Land Conservancy conservation of 145 farmland acres on Hall Road (26-0284), and a sole-source OverDrive library digital content contract (26-0298). Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked the DSS director whether the Duke Energy funding level was consistent with past years, and the director confirmed it typically ranges from $16,000 to $35,000 depending on the time of year; all items were forwarded to the regular session for approval.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Forwarded to regular session without vote

agenda_items.title: Request to Suspend Rules for Budget Ordinance Amendment 26-BCC-086 and TKC Management Services Detention Center Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager requested that the board suspend the rules on a time-sensitive basis to approve Budget Ordinance Amendment 26-BCC-086 (transcribed as '26 VCC086'), appropriating $1,379,000 of general fund balance and authorizing a five-year facility management contract with TKC Management Services at the Durham County Detention Center. A commissioner questioned the transition away from General Services, past internal costs, bidder competition, and early termination options; Manager Hager and the County Attorney confirmed all county contracts permit termination on 30 days' notice, and Sheriff's Office staff noted TKC was the sole bidder and referenced prior contracted maintenance under Aramark from 2000 to 2012 before the video ended mid-discussion at 04:10:42.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deliberated / Recording ended prior to vote

A commissioner moved to enter closed session for the stated reason and another seconded. Chair Lee called for a voice vote without further discussion, and the motion passed unanimously with no opposition voiced.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session May 28, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a budget work session on May 28, 2026, to review FY 2026-27 budget projections, Department of Social Services (DSS) program impacts (including SNAP/FNS and Medicaid work requirements), opioid settlement funding recommendations from the Opioid Settlement Advisory Committee (OSAC), property tax revaluation appeals, and Durham Public Schools (DPS) classified staff salary funding requests. Commissioners discussed the sustainability of local property tax burdens versus state funding shortfalls for school staff and mental health services. No formal votes or motions were taken during this work session.

agenda_items.title: Department of Social Services (DSS) Budget Presentation & Program Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Joanne Pierce and DSS Director Maggie Clap presented the Department of Social Services budget overview for FY 2026-27, highlighting upcoming federal and state funding changes including reductions in Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP) administrative cost reimbursements from 50/50 to 25% federal / 75% county starting October 2026. Commissioners discussed error rates, benefit expenditure drops, and impacts on vulnerable residents.

agenda_items.title: Opioid Settlement Funds & Community Health Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented updates on opioid settlement funds, harm reduction efforts, syringe service distribution, post-overdose response team (PORT) metrics, and the newly launched Durham Opioid Settlement Advisory Committee (OSAC). Co-chair Shalisa Howard Martinez presented OSAC recommendations for FY 2027 funding allocations.

agenda_items.title: General Budget Deliberations & Closing Board Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board discussed overall county budget projections, compensation, capital improvement projects, vehicle replacements, and follow-up items for upcoming budget work sessions, concluding the work session with reminders for the upcoming Monday meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2026-05-26 5:30 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Vice Chair Nida Allam in the absence of Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Board of County Commissioners held its May 26, 2026 regular session with Commissioners Michelle Burton, Stephen Valentine, and Wendy Jacobs present. The board voted unanimously 4-0 by unopposed voice votes to approve the meeting agenda, approve the May 4 work session and May 11 regular meeting minutes, and approve the consent agenda with no items pulled. Sustainability Manager Tobin Freid presented on authorizing Durham County's participation in the North Carolina Commercial Property Assessed Capital Expenditure (C-PACE) program, followed by a public hearing with no speakers signed up and questions from Commissioner Jacobs (with the middle of the transcript truncated before any final C-PACE vote was captured). During the public hearing on the proposed FY 2026-27 county budget, speakers urged at least 1% of Department of Social Services funding for family preservation and reunification, requested funding for a 12% raise for Durham Public Schools classified staff, and criticized commercial tax appeals and occupancy tax allocations, before County Attorney Williamson announced board appointments across several advisory boards with no split or contested votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Land Acknowledgement, Pledge of Allegiance, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nida Allam opened the May 26, 2026 regular session by reading the public charge, after which Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read the land acknowledgement and Commissioner Stephen Valentine led the Pledge of Allegiance. With no adjustments proposed to the agenda, Commissioner Michelle Burton moved to approve the agenda and Commissioner Valentine seconded, passing 4-0 by voice vote with Chair Dr. Mike Lee absent.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Commissioner Comments, and Approval of May 4 and May 11 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace read published announcements including Durham Pre-K 2026-27 applications and Juneteenth commemorations, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs recognized Veteran Services staff member Jonathan Croomes for researching over 300 fallen Durham residents for the Memorial Day ceremony. A commissioner raised a follow-up request to authorize Chair Dr. Mike Lee to send a board letter, noting Lee was absent and deferring the discussion to a future meeting. Commissioner Jacobs then moved and Commissioner Stephen Valentine seconded approval of the May 4 work session and May 11 regular meeting minutes, passing 4-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation: Maternal Mental Health Month and Black Maternal Health Day of Action
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a proclamation recognizing Maternal Mental Health Month and Black Maternal Health Day of Action, hearing remarks from Joy Spencer, Executive Director of Equity Before Birth. Board members thanked Spencer for her advocacy in reducing stigma around help-seeking behaviors and advancing equitable birthing care for Black women and families.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nida Allam asked if any commissioners had questions or wanted to pull items from the consent agenda. Seeing none, the board moved, seconded, and approved the consent agenda 4-0 by unopposed voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Consideration of North Carolina C-PACE Program Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Manager Tobin Freid briefed the board on a resolution authorizing Durham County participation in the North Carolina Commercial Property Assessed Capital Expenditure (C-PACE) program, noting it provides lien-backed financing for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and resilience upgrades with county execution costs reimbursed up to $500 per project. The public hearing opened with no speakers signed up, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked about existing projects in other North Carolina counties and how the state program improved upon models in other states. The remainder of this item occurred during a truncated middle section of the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Not captured in transcript digest (middle truncated)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Proposed FY 2026-27 County Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the public hearing on the proposed county budget (whose opening occurred during the truncated section), Operation Stop CPS speakers and parents criticized Department of Social Services accountability and Family Treatment Court, demanding at least 1% of the department's budget be dedicated to family preservation and reunification. A Durham Public Schools classified staff member urged the board to fund a 12% raise for classified school staff, and another resident argued that commercial property tax appeals, the Blue Ridge tax loophole, and occupancy tax allocations shift revenue burdens onto working residents. Vice Chair Nida Allam closed the public hearing and confirmed with County Manager Hager upcoming budget work sessions on May 28, June 2, and June 4 (if needed), with proposed budget adoption on June 8.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Williamson announced the board's appointment selections across multiple advisory bodies, including Ashley Hillard (Animal Welfare Advisory Board), Dr. Charles Cooperburg, Gracie Johnson Lopez, Ellen Rekow, Dr. Mark Nealey, Dr. Mark Branch, and Ronald Williams (health/hospital and Lincoln Community Health Center positions), Antoinette Day, Glendola Massenberg Beasley, Dan Levine, Crystal Waters, and Antonio Lustre (workforce/employment sector seats), and John Cohen (Farmland Protection Advisory Board). With no items pulled from the consent agenda, Commissioner Michelle Burton moved and Commissioner Stephen Valentine seconded adjournment, which passed by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session May 26, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on May 26, 2026, presided over by Vice Chair Nida Allam. The board approved the agenda, previous minutes, and consent agenda, and unanimously adopted a resolution authorizing county participation in the NC Commercial Property Assessed Capital Expenditure (CPACE) program. Commissioners also heard extensive public comments from educators, staff, and community members regarding DPS classified employee compensation, property tax rates, and family preservation support, and made appointments to various county boards and advisory committees.

agenda_items.title: Opening / Call to Order, Public Charge, & Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Vice Chair opened the work session, read the public charge regarding respectful conduct during board meetings, and Commissioner Jacobs delivered the land acknowledgement honoring indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments & Approval

agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Commissioner Valentine)

agenda_items.title: Announcements & Board Member Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace read upcoming community announcements including Durham PreK applications, hazardous waste disposal events, Durham Hunger Day, Aging & Adult Services events, BRT vision plan, and Juneteenth flag raising. Commissioners also shared personal updates on 529 accounts, Memorial Day ceremonies, and Eid greetings.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes (May 4 and May 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed the draft minutes from the May 4 work session and May 11 regular meeting, noting extensive prior discussion on capital funding assistance to the city, before entertaining a motion for approval.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Jacobs, seconded by Commissioner Valentine)

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joy Spencer, Executive Director of Equity Before Birth, presented proclamations recognizing May as Maternal Mental Health Month and June 10 as Black Maternal Health Day of Action, highlighting maternal health disparities, root causes, and upcoming legislative advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed items on the consent agenda. With no items pulled for separate discussion, a motion was made to approve.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Resolution Authorizing County Participation in NC CPACE Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Manager Tobin Freed presented a public hearing on authorizing Durham County participation in the North Carolina Commercial Property Assessed Capital Expenditure (CPACE) program, which finances energy efficiency and resilience upgrades.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 4-0 (Moved by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Commissioner Jacobs)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2026-27 County Manager Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Hager and Deputy Budget Director David Ades presented the recommended FY 2026-27 budget. Numerous public speakers and union representatives (DAE) raised concerns regarding classified staff wages, property tax appeals, DSS child welfare funding, and school support.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commission Appointments

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Minutes (May 4 and May 11)
votes.discussion_detail: The board reviewed and approved the meeting minutes for the May 4 work session and the May 11 regular meeting. Commissioner Jacobs moved for the approval of both sets of minutes, which was seconded by Commissioner Valentine. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Resolution Authorizing County Participation in NC CPACE Program
votes.discussion_detail: Sustainability manager Tobin Freed presented a public hearing item regarding Durham County's participation in the North Carolina commercial property assessed capital expenditure (CPACE) program. CPACE enables commercial, nonprofit, agricultural, industrial, and multifamily property owners to access financing for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and resilience projects with payments tied to a property lien. Following commissioner discussion confirming similar adoption by Mecklenburg County, the public hearing was closed. Commissioner Burton moved to adopt the resolution authorizing county participation, seconded by Commissioner Jacobs, and the motion passed unanimously with a 4-0 vote.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on May 19, 2026, to review the proposed FY 2026-27 budget overview, tax administration reappraisal impacts, and operational updates from Transportation and the Office of Emergency Services (OES). Staff discussed historically tight revenue growth, commercial property appeals, and resource constraints facing emergency and transit services. No formal votes or policy decisions were taken during this informational work session.

agenda_items.title: FY2026-2027 County Budget Overview & Revaluation Appeals Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff presented the proposed FY27 budget, highlighting severe revenue constraints with only $391,000 in natural property tax growth and $771,000 in sales tax growth. Staff explained the impact of 2025 revaluation appeals exceeding projections by over 3,000 appeals ($2.3 billion lost valuation), and the manager's recommendation for a 2-cent property tax rate increase. Commissioners discussed population growth versus revenue illusions and state/federal funding shifts.

agenda_items.title: Organizational Effectiveness & Performance Measures Companion Document

agenda_items.title: FY2027 Durham Transit Work Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Ellen Beckman and Go Triangle staff presented an update on the final FY27 Durham Transit Work Program. They reviewed challenging revenue forecasts, funding gaps, and the city's request for one-time capital funding for two specific capital projects.

agenda_items.title: Office of Emergency Services Annual Update & EMS Gap Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OES Director Mark Lockhart and Chief Paramedic Kamansky presented department updates and an EMS gap analysis. agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham Library Foundation presented a one-time gift of $117,318 in support of Durham County Library programs. Commissioners and library leadership discussed the vital role of public libraries as community spaces, technology hubs, and resource centers.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Southern School of Energy & Sustainability Boys Basketball State Champions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board honored the Southern School of Energy and Sustainability Boys Basketball Team for winning the 2026 NCHSAA 7A State Championship with a 28-3 record, marking the first state basketball title in school history. Coaches and players shared remarks and posed for photographs.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Southern School of Energy & Sustainability Girls Basketball Team
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized the Southern School of Energy and Sustainability Girls Basketball Team for their outstanding 27-4 season, capturing the Tobacco Road 7A regular season and tournament titles and finishing as state runners-up. Coach Teddy McCoy and players spoke about their historic run.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Beta Pi Sigma Durham Alumni Chapter of Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority 75th Charter Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a resolution honoring the Beta Pi Sigma Durham Alumni Chapter of Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority Inc. on the occasion of its 75th Charter Day, highlighting decades of community service, youth mentorship, and sisterhood in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Declaring Week of the Young Child
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board adopted a resolution recognizing April 2026 as Week of the Young Child in Durham County, emphasizing early childhood education, support for working families, and community investments in young children.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring National Lineman Appreciation Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board adopted a resolution recognizing National Lineman Appreciation Day, thanking Duke Energy linemen and IBEW union representatives for their rigorous training, dedication during storms, and work to modernize electricity and support renewable energy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the consent agenda containing routine administrative and financial items, all of which passed unanimously without items being pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: LGC Application & Bond Order Resolution for GO Refunding Bonds (Series 2026B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a resolution making findings of fact and authorizing the Local Government Commission (LGC) application, introduction of bond order, and calling a public hearing not to exceed $240 million of general obligation refunding bonds (Series 2026B). The board adopted the LGC application resolution.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Calling Public Hearing on Bond Order for April 27, 2026
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered a companion resolution calling a public hearing on the bond order directing a debt statement and statement of disclosure, with the public hearing scheduled for the April 27, 2026 board meeting.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing Modifications to County Property Tax Authority
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered and discussed a resolution opposing legislative or statutory modifications, limits, caps, or freezes to county property tax authority in North Carolina. Commissioners noted that 70% of county revenue supports mandated education, health, and public safety services, and that Durham's property tax rate is at a 55-year low.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session for reasons stated on the agenda, returned to open session with no action taken, and adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Resolution Opposing Modifications to County Property Tax Authority
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham Board of County Commissioners considered and unanimously adopted a resolution opposing any legislative or policy modifications that would restrict, cap, reduce, or otherwise limit county property tax authority. Following the adoption, staff members including Budget and Management Services Director Keith Lane and Tax Administrator Kiar Doul were acknowledged for their work on public transparency. Commissioners highlighted that over the past year, the county has held more than 60 community conversations regarding property taxes, appraisals, and the reevaluation process. Officials also emphasized ongoing public engagement efforts during the budget season, including online feedback portals designed to gather resident priorities amidst shifting local, state, and federal revenues.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session April 6, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on April 6, 2026, reviewing consent items, receiving a financial update on the Durham County Transit Plan, hearing student research presentations from Women NC on the strong black woman archetype, the Medicaid dental 'smile gap' for pregnant women, and Latinx survivors of intimate partner violence, and discussing county detention center medical services and detainee health under the Wellpath contract.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Lee opened the meeting with the public charge, and Commissioner Burton read the land acknowledgement recognizing indigenous peoples including the Catawba, Eno, Occaneechi, Shakori, and Tuscarora nations.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board noted that no speakers had signed up for citizen comments either virtually or in person, and moved forward with the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Manager Hagar presented the consent agenda items, including multiple budget ordinance amendments (Library grants, Public Health dental grants, Cooperative Extension grants, Durham Recovery Court funding) and contract approvals for electrical services, the Junction Road Fleet Operations Project, EMS cardiac monitors and medical supplies, storm water control easements, and sidewalk maintenance agreements. Commissioners asked questions regarding the Junction Road facility site plan alternatives, sustainability/solar features, and the ZOM linear park access.

agenda_items.title: Draft FY 2027 Durham Annual Transit Work Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Paper, Brandy Miner, Curtis Scarpagnado, and Stephen Schlashberg presented the draft FY 2027 Durham Annual Transit Work Program. They reviewed FY 2025 unadjusted financials, sales tax revenues, investment earnings, and transit plan allocations, including discussions on the Ellis Road parcel sale by Go Triangle and transit operating costs.

agenda_items.title: Women NC CEDAW Resolution and Student Research Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Beth Dean (founder and president of Women NC) introduced student researchers Noel Smith (NCCU), Caroline J. (Duke), and Shelina Morgan Lopez (NC State) who presented their research projects on the strong black women archetype in southern communities, the oral health 'smile gap' for pregnant women under Medicaid, and resource access for Latinx survivors of intimate partner violence. Commissioners praised the presentations and discussed the history of Durham's CEDAW resolution.

agenda_items.title: Overview of Medical Services and Detainee Health in the County
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board received an overview of medical services and detainee health in the Durham County Detention Center from Wellpath representatives, Sheriff's office staff, and Public Health Director Dr. Rod Jenkins. Discussions covered contract metrics, outpatient sendouts, chronic care backlogs, mental health care, detox protocols, and systemic integration with justice services and diversion programs.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on March 23, 2026, featuring a ceremonial resolution celebrating 25 years of farmland preservation, a comprehensive FY 2026-27 budget outlook presentation highlighting fiscal challenges and slowing revenue growth, public comments supporting the library system, and board appointments to various advisory boards.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session March 9, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on March 9, 2026. The board recognized the Board of Equalization and Review for managing a historic 10,300 property tax appeals during the 2025 reappraisal cycle, and heard a proclamation for the 52nd annual Durham Crop Hunger Walk. Additionally, the board received a comprehensive staff presentation and unanimously approved selecting Oracle as the county's new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform, authorizing contract negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement & Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Meeting called to order by Chair Mike Lee. Vice Chair Alum read the land acknowledgement, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance. Board approved the agenda as presented.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (28 items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered 28 consent agenda items previously discussed during the budget retreat and work session. Commissioner Burton raised a question regarding the Wellpath contract and jail medical costs before approval.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Creation of Mangum Fire Protection Service District
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on the creation of the Mangum Fire Protection Service District (3.55 square miles, 268 taxable parcels) in the northeast corner of the county. Mark Lockheart (OES Director) presented findings, noting Mariah Volunteer Fire and Rescue Department has provided uncompensated service and can no longer continue without funding. After closing the public hearing, the board adopted the resolution creating the district.

agenda_items.title: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Platform Selection and Contract Negotiations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Greg Merrill and ERP core team presented an update on the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform evaluation. Following a competitive RFP with 9 responses and 3 finalists, staff recommended Oracle as the county's new ERP platform to replace SAP (support ending in 2027). The board authorized staff to move forward with negotiations and implementation planning.

agenda_items.title: Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace presented published announcements including voter photo ID outreach, Creek Week 2026, open space guided nature walks, public safety career exploration camp, conservation educator award, budget survey, and public health extended hours. Commissioners also shared community updates regarding Narcan vending machines and Women's History Month events.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 52nd Annual Durham Crop Hunger Walk
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Proclamation presented for the 52nd annual Durham Crop Hunger Walk. Representatives Alice Sharp and Colleen Herbert spoke about the walk's history and its impact in raising over $5 million for Durham fighting hunger agencies. Commissioners expressed strong support.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (presentation and recognition only)

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (February 9, 2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the regular session minutes from the February 9, 2026 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Board of Equalization and Review Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administration presented recognition for the citizen-led Board of Equalization and Review members who handled a historic 10,300 property tax appeals during the 2025 reappraisal cycle. Commissioners expressed deep gratitude for their intensive service.

votes.item_title: Approval of Oracle ERP Platform Selection and Contract Negotiations
votes.notes: Approved county manager to move forward with contract negotiations to implement Oracle as the county's ERP system replacing SAP.
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered an item regarding the selection of Oracle for the county's new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform and authorizing contract negotiations with DT Solutions. Staff highlighted that the new platform will provide improved integration, enhanced efficiencies, increased internal controls, and significant automation to reduce manual spreadsheet labor. Commissioners inquired about the projected 24-to-36-month implementation timeline, which staff explained was benchmarked against other state and out-of-state counties as well as nearby municipal experiences like the city of Durham. Commissioners also questioned staff regarding staff training inclusions, with staff clarifying that while the current proposal covers the software, comprehensive staff training will be a mandatory requirement in the upcoming implementation partner RFP. Following these discussions, a motion was made and properly seconded to authorize the county manager to move forward with contract negotiations, passing unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session March 2, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on March 2, 2026, featuring public comments opposing a proposed non-contiguous annexation and zoning request outside the urban growth boundary at 4802 Cheek Road. The board received staff updates on economic development incentive performance (highlighting strong return on investment and job creation in life sciences) and on RTP utility infrastructure capital improvement planning and financial affordability. The session also included discussions on a sign-on letter regarding the Duke Energy Carbon Plan before concluding with a closed session and adjournment.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Land Acknowledgement & Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board convened its March 2, 2026 work session with opening remarks, a land acknowledgement read by Commissioner Valentine, and roll call. The board then voted to approve an excused absence for Commissioner Burton due to a schedule conflict.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Proposed Annexation of 4802 Cheek Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens and neighborhood representatives spoke during public comments regarding the proposed annexation and rezoning of 4802 Cheek Road, expressing strong concerns over its location outside the Urban Growth Boundary (UGB), inadequate emergency services (police, fire, EMS response times), environmental impacts on streams and Falls Lake, and incompatibility with rural and agricultural character.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) & Debt Affordability Update

agenda_items.title: Economic Development & Community Partnerships Update
