meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session February 9, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on February 9, 2026, with Chair Dr. Mike Lee presiding. The board approved the agenda (granting excused absences for Commissioners Alam and Valentine), accepted previous meeting minutes, and approved the consent agenda which included investments in farmland protection, open space, and public safety. The board also presented ceremonial resolutions honoring the life and legacy of Judge Willis P. Richard and welcomed newly appointed library director Dana Connors. In public hearings, the board unanimously approved Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendment TC25-02 regarding residential RV parking on driveways, along with the required consistency statement. Finally, the board made numerous routine board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, Pledge of Allegiance, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the regular session, led by Chair Lee. Commissioner Burton read the land acknowledgement and Commissioner Jacobs led the pledge of allegiance. The Board approved the meeting agenda with adjustments.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Agenda approval); also approved excused absences for Commissioners Alam and Valentine at 00:18:11.

agenda_items.title: Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace shared announcements regarding early voting for the 2026 statewide primary and upcoming public hearing notices for the new Unified Development Ordinance (UDO).

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (December 8, 2025, January 5, 2026, and January 12, 2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved three sets of meeting minutes: the December 8, 2025 Regular Session, January 5, 2026 Work Session, and January 12, 2026 Regular Session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Resolution Honoring Judge Willis P. Witchard
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented ceremonial resolutions honoring the life and legacy of Judge Willis P. Witchard, featuring remarks and tributes from commissioners and community members.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Newly Appointed County Board and Commission Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board introduced newly appointed county board and commission members across various advisory boards.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Hagar presented the consent agenda items previously discussed during the work session. Commissioner Jacobs highlighted open space and real estate staff accomplishments regarding land preservation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Adoption of UDO Text Amendment TC25-02 (RV Parking in Residential Districts) and Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Scott Whittman) presented UDO Text Amendment TC25-02 regarding RV parking in residential districts, explaining that the new draft UDO removes restrictions on parking/storing recreational vehicles in side and rear yards, prompting staff to pause current citations. Following public comment closure, the board adopted the text amendment and required consistency statement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Motions for text amendment adoption and consistency statement passage)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved multiple board and commission appointments (Animal Welfare Advisory Committee, Board of Health, Boxing and Wrestling Commission, Durham Convention Center Authority, Women's Commission, Planning Commission, and Historic Preservation Commission).

agenda_items.title: Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board accepted a motion to adjourn the regular session.

votes.item_title: Approval of Agenda (with excused absences for Commissioners Alam and Valentine)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered the approval of the meeting agenda for the regular session, alongside land acknowledgements and public charge readings. Additionally, a motion was introduced and approved for excused absences for Commissioner Alam and Commissioner Valentine. The agenda adjustments and approval passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (December 8, 2025 Regular Session, January 5, 2026 Work Session, and January 12, 2026 Regular Session)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board reviewed and approved the meeting minutes from the December 8, 2025 regular session, the January 5, 2026 work session, and the January 12, 2026 regular session. The motion carried unanimously without further discussion.

votes.item_title: Adoption of UDO Text Amendment TC25-02 (RV Parking in Residential Districts)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board held a public hearing for UDO Text Amendment TC25-02 regarding RV parking in residential districts. With no public commenters signed up, the public hearing was closed by the chair. A motion was then made and seconded to adopt the ordinance amending the unified development ordinance incorporating revisions to article 10 parking and loading, which passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Consistency Statement for UDO Text Amendment TC25-02 (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the close of the public hearing for UDO Text Amendment TC25-02, a second motion was introduced to adopt the required consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. The motion was properly seconded and passed unanimously.

meetings.title: Virtual BOCC Work Session Meeting - February 2, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a virtual work session on February 2, 2026, receiving public comments on Southeast Durham annexations and infrastructure capacity, reviewing the draft City-County Bike-Pedestrian Plan and sidewalk maintenance strategies, hearing an economic development update from the Greater Durham Black Chamber of Commerce, and discussing legislative priorities for the General Assembly short session. The board formally suspended the rules and unanimously approved the consent agenda from the January 26, 2026 regular meeting, which had been canceled due to an ice storm.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the virtual work session, conducted roll call establishing a quorum, and read the public charge and indigenous land acknowledgement.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Four community members spoke during citizen comments regarding ongoing and proposed annexations in Southeast Durham (including 4802 Cheek Road and Patterson Hall), expressing strong concerns about inadequate infrastructure, lack of fire and EMS capacity, environmental degradation, and conflicts with agricultural operations. Commissioners subsequently discussed planning department coordination and the need for comprehensive infrastructure data.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Suspend Rules and Approve January 26, 2026 Regular Meeting Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to the previous week's cancellation of the regular meeting caused by an ice storm, the Board considered suspending its rules to approve the January 26, 2026 Regular Meeting Consent Agenda during the work session. Following discussion, motions were made, seconded, and unanimously approved via roll call.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (5-0) on both motions (suspend rules and approve consent agenda)

agenda_items.title: Work Session Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board proceeded with the consent agenda items scheduled specifically for the February 2, 2026 work session.

agenda_items.title: City-County Bike-Pedestrian Plan and Policy Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the draft City-County Bike-Pedestrian Plan, highlighting methodology, priority projects, and key policy updates regarding regional greenway planning and orphan sidewalk maintenance (such as the Forest View sidewalk near Southern High School). Commissioners praised the collaborative planning effort and discussed maintenance responsibilities and funding options.

agenda_items.title: Update from Greater Durham Black Chamber of Commerce
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CJ Broadick, President and CEO of the Greater Durham Black Chamber of Commerce, presented an update on the organization's partnership, support services for small businesses across startup and scaling phases, and requests for enhanced access to economic development tools and resources. Commissioners engaged in detailed discussion regarding economic development incentives, minority business representation, and future economic strategy.

votes.item_title: Motion to suspend the rules
votes.notes: Motion to suspend rules to allow voting during a work session on items from the canceled January 26 regular meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: During the Durham Board of County Commissioners work session, staff requested that the board suspend its rules to allow for immediate action on items from the previous regular meeting. Following this request, a motion was made and properly seconded to suspend the rules. The roll call vote passed unanimously with 5 affirmative votes.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on January 12, 2026. agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board of Commissioners convened in regular session after holding an earlier closed session with no action taken. The Board reviewed and approved the meeting agenda as presented, and discussed excused absences for Commissioner Wendy Jacobs who was attending a family milestone in Arkansas.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved Agenda (v_bocc_2026_01_12_o7-hws1hqzk_01): Passed unanimously (Unanimous). Excused absence for Commissioner Wendy Jacobs (v_bocc_2026_01_12_o7-hws1hqzk_02): Passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace presented announcements including Durham County government office closures for MLK Jr. Day, the 2026 personal property listing period, voter photo ID outreach events, the joint Martin Luther King Jr. employee observance, and Durham Planning Department office hours.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 1, 2025 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered and approved the minutes from the December 1, 2025 work session.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Recognizing Bull's Life Sciences Academy Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a ceremonial proclamation recognizing Bull's Life Sciences Academy Day in Durham County, celebrating over 200 graduates, life science industry partnerships, and economic mobility pathways supported by Durham County, Durham Tech, and Made in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (minus item 260030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the consent agenda containing 11 items, noting that item 260030 was pulled for separate discussion and vote.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Four public comment speakers addressed the Board on various community topics, concerns, and county governance issues.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Pulled Consent Item 260030

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to adjourn into closed session to discuss matters related to economic development incentives and location or expansion of industries pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4).

agenda_items.title: Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following return from closed session with direction given to staff and no action taken, the Board voted to adjourn the regular session.

votes.item_title: Agenda Approval
votes.discussion_detail: The Board of County Commissioners convened for their regular session, opening with the public charge read by the chair and a land acknowledgement delivered by Commissioner Valentine. Following the pledge of allegiance led by Commissioner Burton, the chair opened the agenda review and approval item. A motion was made and properly seconded to approve the agenda as presented, which passed unanimously with no recorded opposition or nays.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Commissioner Wendy Jacobs
votes.notes: Initially approved, later clarified that virtual attendance allows voting unless tiebreaker.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the agenda approval, the chair introduced a motion for an excused absence for Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, who traveled to Arkansas following the birth of her first grandchild. The motion was moved and properly seconded, passing unanimously. Subsequently, virtual participation rules and voting eligibility were discussed, clarifying that remote commissioners could vote under standard circumstances.

votes.item_title: Approval of December 1, 2025 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the approval of the minutes from the December 1, 2025 work session. A motion was made and properly seconded to approve the minutes as presented. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposing votes.

votes.item_title: Approval of Pulled Item 260030

votes.item_title: Closed Session Motion
votes.notes: Adjourned to closed session pursuant to GS 143-318.11A4 for economic development incentives.
votes.discussion_detail: Following citizen comments regarding family and foster care concerns, the Board considered a motion to adjourn into a closed session pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 143-318.11(a)(4). The motion was moved, properly seconded, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adjournment
votes.notes: Adjourned regular session after returning from closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: After returning from closed session, the presiding official announced that direction was given to staff but no formal action or binding votes were taken during the closed session. A motion to adjourn the meeting was then made, properly seconded, and approved unanimously by the Board.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session December 8, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on December 8, 2025, presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee. The board recognized the 25th anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRY), introduced new Durham County Memorial Stadium Manager Jamal White, and held a public hearing approving a performance-based economic development incentive award of up to $5.5 million for Project Awood and Red Cedar with Novartis Gene Therapies. Additionally, the board approved budget ordinance amendments recognizing SAMHSA grant funds for emergency services EMS opioid response and community donations from Carolina Arbors for the Sheriff's Office K9 unit, before entering a closed session for economic development negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Mike Lee called the meeting to order. The board recited the public charge, an indigenous land acknowledgement, and the pledge of allegiance. The meeting agenda was reviewed and approved without amendments.

agenda_items.title: Information Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk read administrative announcements including Innovate Durham Demo Day, the Durham Soil and Water Conservation District farm law breakfast, the Welcome Baby winter coat drive, property tax partial payment deadlines, LEAP energy assistance applications, and winter holiday office closures. Commissioners also congratulated Habitat for Humanity on their 40th anniversary and upcoming 500th home.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the minutes from the November 3, 2025 work session and November 24, 2025 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of New County Memorial Stadium Manager
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff introduced Jamal White as the new Durham County Memorial Stadium Manager, highlighting his background in sports management and leadership at Duke University. Commissioners welcomed Mr. White and commended his handling of the recent CIAA football championship event.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) 25th Anniversary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Valentine read a resolution recognizing Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) for 25 years of leadership in substance use prevention, opioid overdose response, and community resilience. Dr. Wanda Boon, CEO and co-founder, accepted the resolution and shared remarks.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Non-Emergency Ambulance Franchises
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board held a public hearing regarding non-emergency ambulance franchise applications for multiple medical transport providers, reviewing staff evaluations and public convenience and necessity findings.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Award for Project Aspida Financial Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board held a public hearing on a performance-based economic development award for Project Aspida Financial Services LLC, discussing job creation, capital investment, and community partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Award for Novartis Gene Therapies (Project Awood)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board held a public hearing on a performance-based economic development award up to $5.5 million for Project Awood and Red Cedar (Novartis Gene Therapies), reviewing local workforce pipelines, bioworks certifications, and capital investments.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Williamson presented recommendations for vacant positions on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission and the Farmland Protection Advisory Board, which were approved by the board.

agenda_items.title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC023: SAMHSA Grant for EMS Opioid Response
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC023 recognizing $369,949 in SAMHSA grant funds for the EMS Opioid Response program. Public comment was received regarding homelessness and mental health services, followed by staff presentations clarifying the substance use and community paramedic programs.

agenda_items.title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC038: Carolina Arbors Donations for Sheriff's Office K9
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC038 recognizing $21,347 in community donations from Carolina Arbors for the Sheriff's Office K9 unit. Community members spoke in support of the sheriff's office.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development matters and business location/expansion negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following closed session where no action was taken, the board entertained and approved a motion to adjourn the meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: The Board of County Commissioners convened its regular session on December 8, 2025, with readings of the public charge, land acknowledgement, and pledge of allegiance. After reviewing the agenda and confirming no adjustments or amendments were requested, the board entertained a motion for approval. The meeting agenda was approved unanimously by voice vote without amendments.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Minutes (Nov 3 Work Session and Nov 24 Regular Session)
votes.discussion_detail: Following announcements regarding community events, tax administration options, and a congratulatory recognition of Habitat for Humanity of Durham's 40th anniversary and 500th house, the board considered the approval of meeting minutes. A motion was made and properly seconded to approve the minutes from the November 3, 2025 work session and the November 24, 2025 regular session. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Performance-based economic development award for Project Awood and Red Cedar (Novartis Gene Therapies) up to $5.5M
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered a performance-based economic development award for Project Awood and Red Cedar with Novartis Gene Therapies in an amount not to exceed $5.5 million. Discussions highlighted economic investments creating nearly 1,300 jobs in Durham County and addressed workforce alignment with life science programs. A motion was made and properly seconded to approve the award and authorize the county manager to negotiate and execute the performance agreement. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Amended motion for Aspida Financial Services economic development award
votes.discussion_detail: The chair presented an amended motion for a prior action approving the economic development award for Aspida Financial Services. The amendment explicitly authorized the county manager to negotiate and execute the performance agreement and any related documents necessary to effectuate the board's approval. Following a motion and proper second, the amendment passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC023 (SAMHSA Grant for EMS Opioid Response / $369,949)
votes.discussion_detail: The board addressed board and commission appointments and discussed substance use and mental health response partnerships before considering budget matters. A motion was introduced to approve Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC023 regarding the SAMHSA grant for the EMS opioid response. The motion was properly moved and seconded, and subsequently passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 26BCC038 (Carolina Arbors Community Donations for Sheriff's Office K9 / $21,347)
votes.discussion_detail: This item was pulled from the consent agenda for separate consideration following community engagement. Commissioners expressed gratitude to the Carolina Arbors community for coming together to support the Sheriff's Office K9 unit through donations. Following supportive remarks, a motion was made and seconded, passing unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to enter Closed Session pursuant to GS 143-318.11(a)(4)
votes.discussion_detail: The board proposed entering a closed session to discuss matters related to the location or expansion of industries and other businesses, including negotiating tentative economic development incentives pursuant to General Statute 143-318.11(a)(4). The motion was properly moved and seconded, and approved unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn
votes.discussion_detail: Following a closed session where direction was given to staff with no formal action taken, a motion to adjourn the meeting was accepted. The motion was properly moved and seconded, and passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session December 1, 2025
meetings.presiding_chair: Dr. Mike Lee (Lissa Williamson presiding initially for chair election)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham County Board of County Commissioners held their work session on December 1, 2025. The board elected Dr. Mike Lee as Chair and Nida Alam as Vice Chair for the coming term, and reviewed the consent agenda including budget amendments, EMS equipment purchases, and encumbrance rollovers. Commissioners also heard public comments regarding Department of Social Services child welfare procedures and discussed planning a future work session on DSS processes with judicial and legal stakeholders.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham County Attorney presided over the opening of the December 1, 2025 work session, followed by the land acknowledgment and the nominations and unanimous roll-call elections of Dr. Mike Lee as Board Chair and Nida Alam as Vice Chair, with congratulatory remarks from both leaders.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three community members provided public comments on Department of Social Services operations, no-contact orders, child welfare practices, and community youth programs like Swing Pals.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendy Hager presented consent agenda items including a Carnegie Corporation grant budget ordinance amendment, EMS equipment contracts, a cooperative extension grant, and the FY 25-26 encumbrance rollover.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote recorded during this work session segment

agenda_items.title: Board Discussion on Child Protective Services (CPS) Procedures
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed child welfare procedures, state statutes, and interagency coordination. The board planned a comprehensive presentation for the January work session featuring DSS, the judiciary, and public defenders.

agenda_items.title: Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entertained and approved a motion to adjourn the work session.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair (Dr. Mike Lee)
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Lissa Williamson presided over the opening of the December 1, 2025, work session, noting that under county procedure, the attorney presides until the annual election of the board chair on the first Monday of December. A commissioner nominated Dr. Mike Lee for the position of chair, and no other nominations were made. Following a roll call vote, Dr. Mike Lee was unanimously elected as Board Chair with a 5-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair (Nida Alam)
votes.discussion_detail: Upon assuming the role of chair, Dr. Mike Lee opened the floor for nominations for vice chair. Nida Alam was nominated for the position, with no further nominations brought forward. The clerk conducted a roll call vote, which passed unanimously (5-0) to elect Commissioner Nida Alam as the new Board Vice Chair.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn
votes.discussion_detail: Following board discussions concerning child welfare and plans for a follow-up work session item in January, a motion and second were offered to adjourn the meeting. The chair called for a voice vote on the motion to adjourn, which passed unanimously without opposition. The work session was formally adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session November 24, 2025
meetings.presiding_chair: Chair Nida Allam (Note: Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee and Chair Nida Allam co-led/presided portions, with Nida Allam delivering the State of the County address)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on November 24, 2025. The meeting featured the Annual State of the County Address presented collaboratively by the commissioners and Mayor Leonardo Williams, recognizing achievements across county departments and honoring County Manager Claudia Hager with the Order of the Long Leaf Pine. The board also conducted two public hearings, unanimously approving comprehensive Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendments and a major general rezoning (Z250025) of the entire Research Triangle Park (RTP) to University and College-3 (UC-3) to facilitate a mixed-use, work-live-play vision. Additionally, the board approved a contract with Southern Wall Systems for exterior refurbishment and window replacement at the Durham County Justice Services Center.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, Pledge of Allegiance, and State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the regular session, reciting the public charge, land acknowledgement, and the Pledge of Allegiance. Chair Nida Alam delivered the State of the County Address, highlighting community resilience in response to recent ICE/CBP activity, recognizing new board members and County Manager Claudia Hager (who received the Order of the Long Leaf Pine), and reviewing county achievements and SNAP food drive successes.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Seth Kamansky as Durham County's Chief Paramedic
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Seth Kamansky as Durham County's new Chief Paramedic in the Office of Emergency Services, highlighting his 16 years of experience in Wake County and emergency planning background. Commissioners welcomed him to the county.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing the 75th Anniversary of the Rougemont Ruritan Club
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a commemorative resolution celebrating the 75th anniversary of the Rougemont Ruritan Club, recognizing its extensive community service, roadside cleanups, scholarships, and historic leadership including national presidents Millard Thacker and Lynward Hedgepath.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Private First Class Booker T. Spicely
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Private First Class Booker T. Spicely, a Black World War II soldier killed in Durham in 1944 following a dispute over racial segregation on a bus, joined by civil rights attorney James Williams.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Adjusted)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the adjusted consent agenda, with item 25-0595 pulled for separate public comment and deliberation regarding a contract for the Justice Services Center.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendments (Articles 4, 5, 6, 7) & Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a privately initiated Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendment (TC25001 / RTP 3.0) to amend Articles 4, 5, 6, and 7 to create a new UC3 zoning district facilitating large scientific and technical research parks within the Research Triangle Park. The Board discussed data center definitions and standards before voting.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: RTP Rezoning (Z250025) & Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered a zoning map change request (Z250025) for the Research Triangle Park (RTP) rezoning, aligning with RTP existing covenants and establishing the UC3 zoning district. Following discussion and a consistency statement vote, the rezoning was unanimously approved.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Justice Services Center Exterior Refurbishment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board discussed pulled consent item 25-0595, authorizing a contract with Southern Wall Systems LLC for $1,193,227 for exterior refurbishment and window replacement at the Durham County Justice Services Center. Public comments were heard before the Board unanimously approved the contract.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendments (Article 4, 5, 6, 7)
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered an ordinance amendment incorporating revisions to the unified development ordinance across Article 4 (zoning districts), Article 5 (use regulations), Article 6 (district intensity standards), and Article 7 (design standards). Discussion touched upon limited use standards for new data centers, including distance from residential areas and noise studies, while grandfathering existing facilities. Following discussion, a motion was made and properly seconded to adopt the ordinance amendment. The motion passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendments Consistency Statement
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: Following the adoption of the UDO text amendments, the board took up the required consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. A motion was made and properly seconded to adopt the consistency statement. The motion passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: RTP Rezoning (Z250025)
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: The board addressed the rezoning request (Case Z250025) for the entirety of Research Triangle Park (RTP) except for the Durham County Wildlife Club parcel, covering just over 5,000 acres including rights-of-way. The proposal rezoned the area from various classifications—including science and research park, industrial light, and residential districts—to the newly adopted University and College-3 district. Following staff presentation and discussion regarding comprehensive land use plan alignment and future visioning, a motion to adopt the ordinance amendment was made, seconded, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: RTP Rezoning Consistency Statement
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: In connection with the RTP rezoning request (Z250025), the board considered the adoption of the consistency statement required by North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. A motion was made and properly seconded to adopt the consistency statement. The motion passed unanimously in a voice vote with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: Justice Services Center Exterior Refurbishment Contract
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered agenda item 25-00595, authorizing the county manager to enter into a contract with Southern Wall Systems LLC in the amount of \$1,193,227. The contract provides for exterior refurbishment and exterior window replacement at the Durham County Justice Services Center, along with authority to execute change order amendments as long as funds are available in the CIP fund. Prior to the vote, public comments were received regarding community concerns. Following discussion, a motion was made and properly seconded to approve the item, which passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session November 3, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham County Board of Commissioners held a work session on November 3, 2025, hearing extensive public comment from northern Durham residents regarding concerns over the Durham-to-Roxboro rail-to-trail project. The board suspended rules and unanimously approved grant agreements, budget ordinance amendments, capital project amendments, and a TIP agreement with NC DOT to acquire the 26-mile Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor. Additionally, the board discussed capital improvement plans, debt management, bond ratings, and received presentations on the county's financial outlook and the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) vision plan.

agenda_items.title: Durham-to-Roxboro Rail-to-Trail Acquisition & State Grant Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed public comments opposing the Durham-to-Roxboro rail-to-trail project, followed by a staff presentation and board deliberation on authorizing the chair's signature on the Great Trails State Grant Program agreement ($500,000) and approving capital/budget amendments and TIP agreement with NCDOT for rail corridor acquisition. Commissioners emphasized the long-standing vision, massive outside grant leverage (net local cost of $223,000 or 1.7%), and future transportation preservation.

agenda_items.title: Financial Management & Bond Rating Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board received a presentation and discussed county financial management, debt policies, credit ratings (AAA market access), and investment statutory frameworks with financial consultants and staff.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Vision Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board received an overview and update on the Durham Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Vision Plan from transportation staff and consultants, discussing corridor prioritization and enhanced transit service.

votes.item_title: Suspend rules for consideration of grant and corridor acquisition items
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a procedural motion to suspend the rules to allow for immediate consideration of grant and corridor acquisition items, moving swiftly to advance time-sensitive matters. The motion was moved by Commissioner Burton and seconded by Commissioner Valentine, passing unanimously with no opposing votes. This procedural step preceded discussions and approvals regarding the Great Trails State Grant Program and the Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor acquisition.

votes.item_title: Authorize chair signature on Great Trails State Grant Program agreement ($500,000)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board voted to authorize the chair's signature on the Great Trails State Grant Program agreement with the North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources to accept $500,000 in grant funding. The motion was moved by Commissioner Valentine and seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, passing unanimously. Staff subsequently explained that the funding relates to trail planning and development efforts overseen by the transportation department.

votes.item_title: Approve budget ordinance amendment 26BCC029, capital project amendment 26CPA009, and TIP agreement with NC DOT for Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor acquisition
votes.discussion_detail: The Board approved budget ordinance amendment number 26BCC029, capital project amendment number 26CPA009, and the TIP agreement with the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NC DOT) for the acquisition of the Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor. Transportation Director Ellen Beckman, planner Brooke Roer, and NC DOT manager Hart Evans outlined the project details, noting a total TIP agreement amount of $1,151,445 with a net county expenditure of $223,000 and recognized state grants of $928,445. Staff explained that due to NC DOT's scheduled closing on November 19th, the county was asked to pay the TIP agreement about a week ahead of schedule. The motion was moved by Commissioner Burns and seconded by Commissioner Valentine, and passed unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session October 6, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on October 6, 2025, featuring presentations and discussions on public health updates, opioid fund reallocations, conservation easements, and a comprehensive conceptual overview of the 18.2-mile Durham-to-Roxboro Rail Trail project. The board also reviewed county budget strategies and financial sustainability. No formal votes or contentious policy disagreements occurred during this informational session.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Land Acknowledgement, Resident Comments, and Condolences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened with a land acknowledgement, followed by resident comments regarding county tax increases and governance. Commissioners and the County Manager also shared emotional condolences honoring the life and community legacy of lifelong Durham advocate Devor Langley.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Budget Amendments, Opioid Funds, and Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed consent agenda items including budget ordinance amendments for public health epidemiology expansion, opioid fund reallocation from syringe to naloxone distribution and vending machines, interlocal agreements, electronic test ordering, solid waste planning, and capital project amendments. Special discussion focused on pediatric vaccine availability and opioid settlement fund allocations.

agenda_items.title: Hamlin Reserve Annexation Informational Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented an informational annexation case for Hamlin Reserve (253 and 2523 Hamlin Road, ~42 acres) proposing 81 single-family residences via conservation subdivision outside the urban growth boundary. Commissioners discussed infrastructure impacts, service capacity, and planning consistency.

agenda_items.title: Durham to Roxboro Rail Trail Conceptual Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the comprehensive conceptual plan for the 18.2-mile Durham to Roxboro Rail Trail from Downtown Durham to Person County, covering six segments, trail heads, community connections, funding partnerships, and estimated costs of $46–$57 million with minimal local acquisition costs.

agenda_items.title: County Budget Strategy and Fiscal Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board held a strategic discussion on county budget processes, fiscal sustainability, discretionary versus statutory programs, return on investment for early childhood and support initiatives, and future financial planning amid evolving state and federal burdens.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session September 22, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on September 22, 2025. The board approved the evening's agenda, previous meeting minutes, and several proclamations including Fire Prevention Week focusing on lithium-ion batteries, National Clothing Insecurity Awareness, and Rooted in Wellness Day. Commissioners discussed consent agenda items including capital repairs for Lincoln Community Health Center and a partnership with the RTP Foundation for the sheriff's office, made various board appointments, entered a closed session, and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the regular session, recited the public charge and land acknowledgement, and voted to approve the meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Board and Staff Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners shared announcements regarding the DPS 2025 College Fair, Low-Income Homeowners Relief program (LIHR), municipal primary early voting, extension plant sale, open space grants, Duke Forest deer herd reduction, and Centerfest 50th anniversary.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes (Sept 2 Work Session & Sept 8 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the meeting minutes from the September 2 work session and September 8 regular session without adjustments.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations for Fire Prevention Week, National Clothing Insecurity Awareness, and Rooted in Wellness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Services Director Mark Lockhart presented the Fire Prevention Week proclamation emphasizing lithium-ion battery safety. Proclamations were also recognized for National Clothing Insecurity Awareness and Rooted in Wellness Day.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (RTP Foundation Partnership & Lincoln Community Health Center Repairs)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed consent agenda items including the RTP Foundation partnership for the Sheriff's office space upfit and capital repairs/modernization for Lincoln Community Health Center (HVAC, generator, elevators, parking lots).

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments (Audit Oversight, Discover Durham, Environmental Affairs, Historic Preservation, Memorial Stadium)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Williamson presented board appointments for several committees and authorities, successfully appointing members including Xiao Wu, Jennings Brody, Mark Raiden, Oliver Horton, and Lee Rodeo.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session under General Statutes 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3). Upon returning, no action was taken and the meeting was adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Adjournment passed, 5-0

votes.item_title: Approve minutes from September 2 work session and September 8 regular session

The motion was moved by Commissioner Valentine and seconded by Commissioner Burton (referred to in transcript as Britain), and passed unanimously.

The board also held public hearings and conducted routine administrative and financial business, including contracts for emergency services and property acquisitions. All votes and actions during the session were unanimous.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session September 2, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on September 2, 2025, receiving informational updates from the Farmland Protection Advisory Board on conservation easements and agricultural programs, and a detailed presentation from the Tax Administration department on the 2025 property tax revaluation, appeals process, tax bills, and relief programs. No formal votes or split policy debates occurred during this work session.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval and Conservation Easements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board opened with roll call issues and then reviewed consent agenda items 25-0392 through 25-0483, including real estate lease delegation, medical equipment purchases, DSS and public health budget ordinance amendments, ballot printing services, utility contract amendments, and three conservation easements totaling 342 acres with a county cost of $1.8 million. Commissioner Jacobs praised staff for the conservation easements and highlighted Durham County's milestone as the first in North Carolina to be certified as an entity for the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service Agricultural Land Easement program.

agenda_items.title: Farmland Protection Advisory Board Annual Report and Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheri Scully from Durham Soil and Water and Nicole Connelly, Chair of the Farmland Protection Advisory Board, presented their annual report. They highlighted foundational programs including the Voluntary Agricultural District (VAD) program (with signs built by Southern High School carpentry students), agricultural economic grant programs ($250,000 annually supporting farmers, schools, and nonprofits up to $10,000 per grant), farmland breakfasts, school gardening projects, a partnership with Foothills Regional Commission to update the 2009 Farmland Protection Strategy Plan, and collaboration with the planning department on the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO).
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (presentation and discussion only).

agenda_items.title: 2025 Property Revaluation and Tax Administration Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Dwane Doyle presented an update on the 2025 property revaluation, tax appeals status, tax bills, payment options, and tax relief programs. Doyle reported receiving 10,390 appeals by the June 16 deadline, with 5,090 completed by late August and an aggressive goal to finish by December 1. The board discussed property tax relief programs, including state programs (elderly/disabled homestead exemption, disabled veteran exclusion, and circuit breaker deferment) and the Durham County/City DSS Low-Income Homeowner Relief Program. Commissioners commended Doyle and his staff for their accessibility, consistency, and extensive community outreach during a difficult revaluation cycle.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (presentation and discussion only).

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session August 25th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a regular session on August 25, 2025. The board approved salary adjustments for positions reporting to the board, excused Commissioner Jacobs' absence, and approved the agenda, minutes, and consent agenda unanimously. Additionally, the board proclaimed September as National Preparedness Month, honored the late Thomas Henry Krakow, unanimously passed a resolution supporting state funding for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), discussed a public hearing regarding the naming request for the William V. Bill Bell lobby (to be re-noticed for September 8th), and made appointments to the Alliance Board of Directors and Environmental Affairs Board.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and made appointments for vacancies on the Alliance Board of Directors and the Environmental Affairs Board.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 on motion to adjourn after selections.

agenda_items.title: Salary Changes for Positions Reporting to the Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board discussed and approved salary changes for positions reporting directly to the Board of Commissioners following closed session evaluations, including increases for the clerk, county attorney, chair, commissioners, manager, register of deeds, and tax administrator.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 on motion by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Commissioner Jacobs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered and approved an excused absence for Commissioner Jacobs from the regular session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 on motion by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, seconded by Commissioner Valentine.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval & Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved the meeting agenda with announcements regarding upcoming Labor Day office closures.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 on motion by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, seconded by Commissioner Burton.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved the meeting minutes from the August 4 work session and August 11 regular session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 on motion by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, seconded by Commissioner Burton.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed proclamations and presentations, including recognition of community milestones and leadership.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved the consent agenda without items pulled by commissioners.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 on motion by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting State Funding for SNAP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board debated and passed a resolution supporting state funding for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and addressing SNAP education funding.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearings & Board Discussions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board conducted public hearings on naming and facility policies, discussing proper noticing requirements and community recognition.

votes.item_title: Salary Changes for Positions Reporting to the Board
votes.notes: Approved salary increases including clerk (12.91%), county attorney (10.42%), manager (6.78%), tax administrator (12.126%), chair (3.36%), commissioner (1.4%), and register of deeds (1.127%).
votes.discussion_detail: Following a closed session for board evaluations, the board considered proposed salary adjustments for positions reporting directly to the Board of Commissioners. The announced increases included 12.91% for the Clerk to the Board, 10.42% for the County Attorney, 3.36% for the Chair, 1.4% for Commissioners, 6.78% for the Manager, 1.127% for the Register of Deeds, and 12.126% for the Tax Administrator. The motion to approve these salary changes was moved by Commissioner Michelle Burton, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee, and approved unanimously by a 4-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Commissioner Jacobs
votes.notes: Commissioner Jacobs excused from the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Prior to proceeding with the public charge and meeting proceedings, a motion was introduced to formally grant an excused absence for Commissioner Jacobs. The motion was moved by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Commissioner Stephen Valentine. The motion passed unanimously (4-0).

votes.item_title: Agenda Approval
votes.discussion_detail: Following the pledge of allegiance and opening remarks, the board checked for any adjustments to the proposed meeting agenda. Hearing no requested changes, Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved for approval of the agenda with a second from Commissioner Michelle Burton. The agenda was unanimously adopted (4-0) by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Approved August 4 work session and August 11 regular session minutes.
votes.discussion_detail: The board reviewed two sets of meeting minutes for approval, covering the August 4th work session and the August 11th regular session. votes.item_title: Resolution Supporting State Funding for SNAP
votes.notes: Resolution calling upon the North Carolina General Assembly to approve estimated $420 million annual state budget appropriation for SNAP.
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham Board of County Commissioners considered a resolution supporting state funding for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), which serves approximately 13% of households in North Carolina (totaling 1,357,112 participants statewide and 32,660 in Durham County as of July 2025). The motion for approval was moved by Commissioner Stephen Valentine, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee, and unanimously passed with a 4-0 vote. Following the vote, Commissioner Valentine began reading the resolution details into the record, noting that four out of five participating families include a child, senior, or adult with a disability, and that every dollar in SNAP benefits generates $1.50 to $1.80 for local economies.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session August 4th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on August 4, 2025, reviewing consent agenda items and receiving briefings on federal Medicaid and SNAP policy impacts, Alliance Health's provider network and Durham Public Schools mental health programming, and the Golden Leaf Foundation Community-Based Grants Initiative endorsement process. Commissioners discussed communication gaps between Alliance Health and DPS, hazard mitigation planning following recent storms, and strategies to maximize external grant funding. No formal votes were conducted during the work session.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Land Acknowledgement & Resident Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board convened its work session with the public charge read by staff and a land acknowledgement delivered by Commissioner Valentine. Staff noted that no individuals signed up for resident comments, allowing the meeting to proceed directly to the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approvals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Hager presented consent agenda items, including stadium bleacher replacements, a $1.5M budget amendment for the affordable housing loan fund partnering with Self-Help and Duke University, sheriff vehicle equipment purchases, highway safety and hazard mitigation grants, utility engineering services, the annual transit work plan, and the Community Schools program contract with Student U. Commissioners discussed vehicle supply chain backlogs, hazard mitigation planning in the wake of Tropical Storm Chantal, and reporting requirements for community school and transit programs.

agenda_items.title: County Grant Landscape & Federal Medicaid/SNAP Changes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS Director Maggie Clap presented an update on federal policy changes impacting Medicaid and SNAP (food and nutrition services), detailing proposed work requirements, six-month recertification mandates, and provider tax limitations threatening Medicaid expansion in North Carolina. Commissioners discussed local enrollment numbers in Durham, economic impacts, and legislative advocacy efforts.

agenda_items.title: Alliance Health Provider Network & Behavioral Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Alliance Health representatives presented an update on their provider network, highlighting partnerships with Lincoln Community Health Center, El Futuro, and Carolina Outreach, as well as school-based behavioral health initiatives and forensic support services for re-entering individuals. Commissioners raised concerns regarding coordination and communication with Durham Public Schools (DPS) and discussed sustainable funding strategies for upstream mental health programs.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on July 28, 2025, addressing emergency management and program integrity proclamations, public comments on land tax assessments, and staff recognitions for national achievement awards. The board approved the consent agenda, authorized the FY 2025-26 economic development contract with Downtown Durham Inc., and made numerous board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened its regular session in a new meeting space (Health and Human Services building, 2nd floor) due to HVAC issues in the admin one building. The meeting opened with the public charge read by the chair and a land acknowledgement given by Commissioner Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed agenda adjustments and adopted the meeting agenda following a motion and unanimous vote.

agenda_items.title: County Announcements and Recognitions

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 23, 2025 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the minutes for the June 23, 2025 regular session, incorporating a correction noted by Commissioner Jacobs regarding a vote record.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the public provided comments on various county issues, tax assessments, land valuation appeals, and community concerns.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of NACo Achievement Awards and Digital Cities Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Hager and the commissioners recognized county staff and departments for winning 11 National Association of Counties (NACo) achievement awards and a 2025 Digital Cities survey award.

agenda_items.title: School Capital Projects and Facilities Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented updates and discussed school capital projects, funding allocations, and facility improvements, including the planned academy at Southern High School.

agenda_items.title: Agricultural Conservation Easements and Land Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed land conservation easements and agricultural preservation, highlighting contributions from local farming families and watershed protection around Falls Lake.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the consent agenda, including routine grants and contracts such as a library foundation grant award.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Contract with Downtown Durham Inc. for Economic Development Services ($200,000)

agenda_items.title: Adjournment

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on June 23, 2025, approving meeting minutes, the agenda, and the consent agenda. Commissioners also made numerous appointments to various county boards and commissions, noting a couple of ties that will be resolved at the next meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement

agenda_items.title: Clerk Announcements and Board Member Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace announced upcoming convenience site closures, the Deco Does Pride event, Durham Cultural Roadmap feedback sessions, opioid overdose prevention training, meals on wheels box fan drive, and the Durham This Week newsletter. Board members shared personal reflections on prostate cancer awareness, Durham Refugee Day celebration, and the passing of community recovery advocate Dennis Garrett.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes for June 2nd Work Session and June 9th Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the minutes from the June 2nd work session and June 9th regular session.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda

agenda_items.title: Presentation of the Fiscal Year 2024 Comprehensive Financial Report Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim CFO Crystal Wright and Scott Anderson from Cherry Bekaert presented the FY 2024 annual comprehensive financial report audit. The auditors reported issuing an unmodified opinion, the highest level of assurance, noting strong internal controls and proper financial reporting.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Williamson presented numerous board and commission vacancies and appointments across various advisory boards, commissions, and committees. Appointments were made for all vacant positions except for the Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees and Sports Commission, where ties occurred and were carried over to the next meeting.

votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the approval of the meeting minutes for the June 2nd work session and the June 9th regular session. meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session June 9th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on June 9, 2025, where they unanimously approved the FY 2025-26 annual budget, budget fee schedule, annual opioid settlement fund ordinance, and related spending resolutions. The board also approved the meeting agenda and previous minutes, heard extensive community presentations and proclamations (including Juneteenth, Pride Month, Women Veterans Day, World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, and Durham Refugee Day), recognized NCCU Chancellor Dr. Carrie G. Dixon and budget art contest winner Zora Williams, and adjourned to closed session before concluding the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Land Acknowledgment, Pledge, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Meeting convened with public charge, land acknowledgment by Commissioner Valentine, pledge of allegiance led by Commissioner Jacobs, and approval of the meeting agenda. Clerk Wallace and commissioners shared community announcements regarding Juneteenth, firearm injury prevention, and voter ID outreach.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 27th Board Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the minutes from the previous meeting on May 27th, 2025.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved May 27th Board Minutes (v_bocc_2025_06_09_y_hb3JbAaUQ_02) passed, unanimous (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentations, Proclamations, and Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ceremonial recognitions and proclamations including the budget book cover art contest winner Zora Williams, Women's Veterans Day 2025, World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, Juneteenth and Pride Month proclamations, Durham Refugee Day, and a resolution honoring NCCU Chancellor Dr. Carrie G. Dixon.

agenda_items.title: Adopt FY 2025-26 Budget, Fee Schedule, and Budget Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presentation, public discussion, and adoption of the FY 2025-26 annual budget, fee schedule, and tax rate increase of 3.5 cents over the revenue-neutral rate. Commissioners discussed funding for Durham Public Schools, local employee compensation, capital improvements, and broader fiscal constraints.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, unanimous (5-0) for adopting the fee schedule, budget ordinance, and related measures.

agenda_items.title: Adopt FY 2025-26 Opioid Settlement Fund Resolution and Budget Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Adoption of the FY 2025-26 annual opioid settlement fund resolution and annual budget ordinance for opioid settlement funds, following opioid town hall updates and management reports.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, unanimous (5-0) for both the Opioid Settlement Fund Resolution and the Opioid Settlement Budget Ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Regular Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to adjourn into closed session pursuant to NC General Statute 143-318.11(a)(5), returning later to adjourn the regular meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, unanimous (5-0) to adjourn to closed session and later adjourn regular session.

votes.item_title: Approve Meeting Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: The Board of Commissioners convened for their regular session on Monday, June 9th, beginning with the public charge and a land acknowledgement delivered by Commissioner Valentine honoring indigenous peoples including the Catawba, Eno, Shakori, and Tuscarora. Commissioner Jacobs led the Pledge of Allegiance before Clerk Wallace presented routine announcements regarding Durham County office closures for Juneteenth, the 25th anniversary of the Durham County Firearm Injury Prevention Partnership, free voter ID outreach events, and public feedback opportunities for the new unified development ordinance (UDO). Following these announcements, the agenda was unanimously approved 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Burton and seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee.

votes.item_title: Approve May 27th Board Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the adoption of the May 27th board minutes amidst public comments on the proposed FY 2025-26 budget ordinance. Several public speakers, including teachers and county residents, addressed the board regarding teacher pay supplements, economic uncertainties, and county financial management. Following public comments, the board reviewed and voted on administrative business.

votes.item_title: Adopt FY 2025-26 Budget Fee Schedule
votes.discussion_detail: The board addressed the adoption of the fee schedule for the FY 2025-26 budget after thanking County Manager Hager and budget staff for their detailed analysis, long hours, and careful management in a tough economic climate. Commissioner Jacobs moved to adopt the budget fee schedule, which was seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee and passed unanimously 5-0 with no dissenting votes.

votes.item_title: Adopt FY 2025-26 Annual Opioid Settlement Fund Resolution
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the adoption of the annual opioid settlement fund resolution and related spending resolutions for FY 2025-26. Commissioner Valentine moved approval of the resolution, which was seconded by Commissioner Burton and passed unanimously 5-0. Following the vote on the resolution, the board proceeded to consider the accompanying budget ordinance for the opioid settlement funds.

votes.item_title: Adopt FY 2025-26 Annual Budget Ordinance for Opioid Settlement Funds
votes.discussion_detail: The board took up the fiscal year 2026 annual budget ordinance for opioid settlement funds following the adoption of the settlement fund resolution. Commissioner Valentine moved approval of the budget ordinance for opioid settlement funds, which was seconded by Dr. Lee and passed unanimously by a 5-0 vote. Afterward, the board voted to adjourn into closed session pursuant to General Statute 143-318.115.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: During the regular session, the board moved through final budget fee schedule adoption and the annual opioid settlement fund ordinance and spending resolutions before considering a closed session. Following these items, a motion was made by Commissioner Burton and seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee to adjourn into closed session pursuant to General Statute 143-318.115. The motion passed unanimously (5-0) with no recorded nays or opposition.

votes.item_title: Adjourn Regular Session
votes.discussion_detail: Following the conclusion of the closed session where staff received direction and no formal action was reported, the board reconvened briefly. Commissioner Burton moved to adjourn the regular session, which was seconded by Commissioner Jacobs. The motion passed unanimously (5-0) with no opposition, officially adjourning the meeting.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: FY 2025-26 Budget Ordinance Adoption: DPS Increase Beyond Manager's Recommendation & Praise for Manager Hager
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: Manager Hager closed out her first budget as permanent County Manager, noting the $55M initial gap and unprecedented federal/economic uncertainty, while thanking the Board for trusting staff and keeping the final adopted tax rate at her recommended 3.5-cent increase.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Burton warmly thanked Manager Hager for answering her calls at all hours and on weekends during her first budget cycle. While noting the Board went $2.57M beyond Hager's recommended DPS funding (plus $10M one-time capital), she emphasized the Board collaborated with staff to hold Hager's recommended 3.5-cent tax increase.
member_positions.key_quote: And finally to our county manager Claudia Hager for meeting with me, answering my calls at all hours of the night and weekends when I had questions about the budget and how we could creatively find resources.

member_positions.stance_summary: Vice Chair Lee praised Manager Hager and staff for their patience with new commissioners and for executing the financial adjustments needed to add $2.5M above the initial DPS recommendation while keeping the tax increase at Hager's 3.5-cent recommendation.
member_positions.key_quote: And I deeply appreciate the work that the staff and the county manager did, the gymnastics that was able to be done to add $2.5 million on to the initial recommendation.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Valentine thanked Manager Hager and her team for easing his learning curve as a new commissioner, praising the adopted budget as a fiscally smart reset in an uncertain federal climate that funded DPS and pre-K without exceeding the recommended 3.5-cent tax burden.
member_positions.key_quote: So, county manager, your entire team across government, thank you, and so as a new county commissioner, I can definitely say that you have helped the learning curve thus far.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs thanked Manager Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane for providing the guidance and data that allowed the Board to stay on solid financial ground, add $2.75M above Hager's proposed DPS funding (while trimming Hayti Reborn to $500K), and keep the tax increase at 3.5 cents.
member_positions.key_quote: Thank you, Manager Hager and Durham County staff for the guidance, expertise, and information you provide to us as elected officials to help us make the most informed decisions possible.

member_positions.stance_summary: Chair Allam congratulated Manager Hager on completing her first budget as permanent (rather than interim or acting) County Manager, praising her 'strength, care, and clarity' and noting that Hager proactively instructed departments to submit tightened budgets amid tough economic headwinds.
member_positions.key_quote: I really just want to take a huge moment to extend not just thanks but congratulations to county manager Hager because this is her first budget as our permanent county manager, not just as interim or acting, and she truly led us through this process with so much strength, care, and clarity.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session June 3rd, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its fifth budget work session for the FY 2025-2026 budget on June 3rd, 2025, focusing on reviewing the add/delete list, closing budget gaps without a property tax increase, and discussing the budget ordinance provisions regarding school funding and financial transparency. Commissioners discussed allocations for Durham Public Schools (DPS), Alliance Health funding, and community partner organizations such as Hayti Reborn, ultimately aligning on a balanced approach to be voted on for adoption on June 9th. No formal roll-call vote or motion was recorded during this specific work session transcript (it was a continuation work session ending in adjournment).

agenda_items.title: Budget Work Session Add/Delete List Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Manager Hagar and budget staff reviewed day five of the budget work session, focusing on the add/delete list adjustments. They discussed administrative updates, including Pre-K hold-harmless funding and new revenues, and balancing the budget without a property tax increase.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools (DPS) Funding & Capital Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed allocations for Durham Public Schools (DPS), specifically reducing ongoing capital from $6 million to $5 million while considering additional funds for transportation and exceptional children (EC) services, alongside Pay-Go funds and LOBs.

agenda_items.title: Community Partner Funding and Hayti Reborn Allocation Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed funding allocations for community partner programs such as Hayti Reborn, debating operational versus programmatic expansion needs, and contrasting local funding priorities.

agenda_items.title: Budget Ordinance Modifications and School Financial Reporting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the proposed budget ordinance modifications, reporting requirements, and charter school financial reporting structures to ensure increased transparency and accountability.
