meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session June 2nd, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a budget work session on June 2nd, 2025, focusing on key community and justice system topics. The board discussed school truancy processes and court system dynamics with District Attorney Satana Deberry, noting challenges with absenteeism and rising detention numbers. Additionally, the board reviewed funding, operations, and community intervention programs with representatives from Hey Tai Reborn (Hey Tai / HRJM).

agenda_items.title: Durham County District Attorney Discussion: Truancy and Court Case Flow
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District Attorney Satana Deberry joined the board to discuss truancy processes and court case backlogs and detention numbers. DA Deberry clarified that Durham has never had a formal truancy court, and attendance letters are now handled under the superintendent's signature rather than the DA's. The board and DA also discussed rising detention center populations, pending homicide cases, and the need for interagency collaboration to address chronic absenteeism and youth crime.

agenda_items.title: Hey Tai Reborn Justice Movement Update and Budget Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Executive Director LA Jones and Program Director Steve Chambers presented an update on the Hey Tai Reborn Justice Movement community intervention programs, detailing their wraparound services, bridge programs with Durham Tech, and client demographics. Commissioners engaged in extensive deliberation regarding ongoing county funding, historical ARPA allocations, salary and operational sustainability, and county budget constraints amid an austerity budget cycle.

agenda_items.title: Add/Delete Review and Budget Reconciliation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff and commissioners reviewed the add/delete list for the proposed budget, discussing potential adjustments such as modifying DPS current expense and capital allocations, vehicle budgets, and adjusting funding levels for community agencies like Hey Tai Reborn to balance the county budget. Commissioners debated various trade-offs and reconciled remaining budget gaps.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session June 2nd, 2025
disagreements.issue: Funding and sustainability of Hey Toronto / Hey Tai Reborn community intervention programs vs county budget constraints
disagreements.summary: Discussion and debate on funding levels, sustainability, and financial transparency for Hey Tai Reborn community intervention services during budget work sessions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Skeptical of ongoing operational support without strict data, clear financials, and long-term sustainability plans amidst austerity.
side_a_arguments: County commissioners (e.g. Commissioner Jacobs) raised concerns over accountability, high salary proportions, and lack of sustainability for ongoing operational funding as ARPA funds expire.
disagreements.side_b_position: Urged ongoing financial support and partnership to sustain vital community work for vulnerable populations.
side_b_arguments: Representatives from Hey Tai Reborn and commissioners supporting them argued that grassroots organizations provide crucial community interventions, wraparound services, and second chances that county entities cannot duplicate.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioners questioned financial allocations and sustainability of grassroots nonprofit funding given upcoming county budget austerity and expiration of ARPA funds, while acknowledging the organization's value and agreeing to consider partial funding.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: Low-Income Homeowner Relief (LIHR) Budget Follow-Up Memo Discrepancy
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: Manager Hager acknowledged an inadvertent error in the budget and management follow-up memo that listed FY 2025-26 Low-Income Homeowner Relief (LIHR) funding at $500,000 total ($250K city / $250K county) instead of maintaining the $500,000 county base level, committing to correct it.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs caught a $500,000 discrepancy in the budget and management follow-up response regarding the Low-Income Homeowner Relief program, pointing out that the county had already spent ~$800,000 year-to-date and was supposed to maintain base funding. Manager Hager admitted the error and thanked Jacobs for keeping staff on their toes.
member_positions.key_quote: Just so you know, I do read.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: FY 2025-26 Budget Work Session: Override of Manager's DPS & Hayti Reborn Proposals, Vehicle Budget & Tax Rate
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: To cover the Board's requested +$2.574M addition to DPS above her recommended budget, Manager Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane proposed shifting $1M from DPS capital to current expense, leaving a $1.4M gap (or $900K with a $500K Hayti Reborn cut requiring a +0.1-cent tax increase); Hager also defended keeping vehicle replacements intact due to tariff pricing risks.

member_positions.stance_summary: Chair Allam challenged the math of shifting $1M from DPS capital to current expense due to charter school pass-throughs, demanding confirmation from DPS and management that salary increases would not dip into charter fees. She also directly opposed Manager Hager's $1M recommended allocation for Hayti Reborn Justice Movement, citing inadequate outcome justification and calling for its complete removal.
member_positions.key_quote: My preference is that we remove that funding from this budget cycle.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Burton echoed Allam's concern about verifying DPS's charter surcharge calculations given past miscalculations, and proposed modifying Manager Hager's $1M recommendation for Hayti Reborn down to $500,000 for continuation only so the organization could develop a self-sustainability plan.
member_positions.key_quote: I would be willing to give them 500,000, I don't think they need the whole amount, but maybe 500,000 to continue operations.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs backed Burton's $500,000 reduction to Hayti Reborn, pushed back against Manager Hager's refusal to trim the vehicle replacement budget to close the DPS gap, and signaled she would not go beyond a 3.6-cent tax rate increase.
member_positions.key_quote: So going back to the vehicles budget, there wasn't any area that you all felt like we could decrease a little bit?

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Valentine expressed strong reluctance to raise property taxes beyond the Manager's 3.5-cent recommendation in light of the reappraisal, and reluctantly agreed to cut Hayti Reborn from $1M to $500K despite his support for the program because the math helped solve the DPS funding gap.
member_positions.key_quote: In light of the reappraisal and the current environment we're in, I'm just not comfortable with raising taxes in this environment.

member_positions.stance_summary: Vice Chair Lee withheld support from his colleagues' move to cut Manager Hager's $1M Hayti Reborn recommendation, warning that cutting Hayti Reborn on top of eliminating Bull City United amounted to piecemeal divestment from programs serving Black and brown residents and youth.
member_positions.key_quote: If we continue to divest throughout Durham, there's not going to be anything left and I fear for that.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session May 29th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a budget work session on May 29, 2025, to review budget requests and financial updates from Durham Public Schools, the Department of Public Health, and the Durham County ABC Board. Commissioners discussed school funding priorities (including local teacher supplements, bus driver pay, and exceptional children services), public health impacts from federal grant reductions, and ABC Board revenues and community grants. No formal policy votes or budget adoptions occurred during this work session.

agenda_items.title: Election of Temporary Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In accordance with rules and procedures, since both Chair Alam and Vice Chair Dr. Lee are absent, the board opens the floor for nominations for a temporary chair. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs is nominated, seconded, and unanimously elected as temporary chair to preside over today's budget work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously by voice vote (Mover/Seconder: Nomination of Commissioner Jacobs).

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Budget Presentation & Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis and CFO Jeremy Teter present the Durham Public Schools (DPS) budget request and update on 100-day listening/learning sessions. They discuss a $900M facility needs estimate, HVAC system maintenance/repair issues, bus driver recruitment successes (adding 40 drivers since January), and financial transparency/internal deficit resolution.

agenda_items.title: Department of Public Health Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Rod Jenkins and staff present the Durham County Department of Public Health budget request, detailing revenue generation, local grants, federal funding challenges (including cuts to tobacco prevention, HIV/STI testing, and the award-winning Dine nutrition education program), and the lab services agreement with Orange County.

agenda_items.title: Durham County ABC Board Budget Presentation & Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County ABC Board representatives present their annual budget, store modernization updates (including new stores on Glenn School Road and Hope Valley, and a future warehouse project on Hoover Road), working capital, and community grants to local nonprofits. Commissioners discuss sales trends, tequila market dominance, staff wages, and fund balances.

agenda_items.title: Board Discussion on Budget Priorities, School Funding, and Reallocations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members engage in a detailed deliberation on the overall county budget, balancing requests from Durham Public Schools (teacher supplements, bus drivers, exceptional children), Hattie Reborn funding, and property tax considerations. Commissioners discuss potential funding reallocation and review follow-up items for the upcoming Monday session.

agenda_items.title: Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Valentine moves to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Commissioner Burton. The motion passes by unanimous voice vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously by voice vote (Mover: Commissioner Valentine, Seconder: Commissioner Burton).

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session May 27th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on May 27, 2025, presided over by Chair Nida Alam. The meeting featured proclamations for Jewish American Heritage Month, Asian-American Pacific Islander Heritage Month, and National Foster Care Month, followed by extensive public comments urging full funding for Durham Public Schools ($16 million request), countywide expansion of the HEART mental health response program, and funding for early legal defense for child welfare families. The board also made multiple board and commission appointments and unanimously approved pulled consent agenda items (25-0266 and 25-0289) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to GS 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board convened in closed session to discuss matters related to general statutes 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6). No action was taken during the closed session, and the board subsequently motioned to come out of closed session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (motion to enter/exit closed session passed unanimously)

agenda_items.title: Public Charge & Indigenous Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Alam opened the meeting and reviewed the public charge regarding respectful courteous conduct. Commissioner Burton led the indigenous land acknowledgement recognizing the Catawba, Eno, Occaneechi, Shakori, and Tuscarora peoples.

agenda_items.title: County and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace and board members shared community announcements including Wear Orange Day for gun violence awareness, the 2025 real property tax appeal deadline, Redwood Convenience site closure, DPS summer meal programs, opioid settlement community meeting, and the Juneteenth flag raising ceremony. Commissioner Jacobs highlighted the Bulls Academy life sciences certification program.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes for May 5 Work Session and May 12 Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from the May 5 work session and May 12 regular session. Hearing no adjustments, a motion for approval was made by Commissioner Burton and seconded by Commissioner Valentine.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (voice vote, mover: Commissioner Burton, seconder: Commissioner Valentine)

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Jewish American Heritage Month, AAPI Heritage Month, and National Foster Care Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented three proclamations: Jewish American Heritage Month (presented by Commissioner Jacobs with remarks from Raina Goldstein Banug on tikkun olam), Asian American Pacific Islander Heritage Month (presented by Commissioner Burton with remarks from Dr. Lewis), and National Foster Care Month (presented by Commissioner Valentine with remarks from DSS Director Clap emphasizing family reunification).
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (proclamations and presentations only)

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Agenda and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the meeting agenda, pulled two consent agenda items (25-0266 and 25-0289) for separate discussion/public comment, and approved the agenda. The board also approved an excused absence for Vice Chair Dr. Lee.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (voice vote, mover: Commissioner Jacobs, seconder: Commissioner Burton)

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 25-0266 and 25-0289)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the consent agenda items, noting that items 25-0266 and 25-0289 were pulled. Commissioner Jacobs highlighted the animal shelter item moving forward, and the remaining consent agenda items were approved.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 4-0 (motion by Commissioner Jacobs, second by Commissioner Burton)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 25-0266 (Sheriff Vests) & 25-0289 (Animal Shelter Contract) & Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters (Amanda Wallace, Antoanet Haw, and Rafi Zadei) spoke on pulled consent items 25-0266 ($125,775 for Sheriff protective vests) and animal shelter funding, questioning spending priorities relative to community needs and violent crime rewards.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote during public comment portion (discussion only)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2025-26 County Manager Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board opened a public hearing on the FY 2025-26 county manager recommended budget. Numerous community members, teachers, bus drivers, social workers, and advocates testified regarding full funding for Durham Public Schools ($16 million request), property tax reappraisal impacts on seniors, expansion of the HEART unarmed response program, and holistic early defense representation (Carolina Parent Defenders).
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (public hearing / testimony only)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Williamson presented board and commission appointment recommendations across multiple committees, including the Audit Oversight Committee, Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees, Durham Racial Equity Commission, Durham Workforce Development Board, and Memorial Stadium Authority. The board congratulated all appointees.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Pulled Consent Agenda Items 25-0266 and 25-0289
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board returned to consider the two pulled consent agenda items (25-0266 regarding sheriff protective vests and 25-0289 regarding animal shelter contract). A motion to approve both items was made by Commissioner Jacobs and seconded by Commissioner Burton.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 4-0 (motion by Commissioner Jacobs, second by Commissioner Burton, voice vote recorded as 4-0)

agenda_items.title: Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a long meeting, a motion to adjourn was made by Commissioner Valentine and seconded by Commissioner Jacobs. All members voted in favor.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (motion by Commissioner Valentine, second by Commissioner Jacobs)

votes.item_title: Approval of pulled consent agenda items 25-0266 and 25-0289
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Jacobs moved to approve pulled consent agenda items 25-0266 and 25-0289, with a second by Commissioner Burton. Prior to the vote, public comments included testimony from Durham public school teachers urging full funding of the DPS budget request to avoid cuts to frontline positions and raises. The board also reviewed various board and commission appointments before taking up the pulled consent items, which passed unanimously with a 4-0 vote.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session May 22th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: On day two of its FY26 budget work session, the Board of County Commissioners heard budget presentations and operational updates from the Office of the Sheriff, the Office of Emergency Services (OES), and the Durham County Youth Home. Commissioners questioned department leaders extensively on fleet replacement costs and tariff impacts, 89 detention officer vacancies and mandatory overtime, rising EMS call volumes and response times, Medicaid Tailored Plan billing delays, and aligning growth planning with emergency service capacity. No formal motions or votes were taken during this work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Office of the Sheriff Law Enforcement Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened day two of the budget work session and invited Sheriff Clarence Birkhead to present. Before beginning the budget overview, Captain Carpenter updated the board on the apprehension of a suspect in a recent Red Mill Road homicide, and Captain Webster described Durham deputies assisting Chatham County during a nine-hour standoff on an involuntary commitment call. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Michelle Burton, and Stephen Valentine asked about response protocols for mental health histories, prior calls at the residence, and community intelligence used in the arrest.

agenda_items.title: Office of the Sheriff FY26 Budget Presentation and Detention Center Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Birkhead presented FY26 budget priorities, highlighting recommended funding for 34 EcoBoost SUVs and fleet replacements, a $343,200 vehicle maintenance increase, and five new deputy positions for an RTP zone funded via position realignment, alongside unfunded requests including detention center kitchen repairs, stab-resistant vests, Cellbrite, uniforms, BeyondTrust IT software, and additional training. Commissioners pressed staff on vehicle replacement lifecycles, factory recalls, tariff price projections, the estimated $500,000 RTP tax district contribution, HEART co-response expansion resourcing, and jail food service contracting. Significant discussion also focused on the detention center's 89 vacancies out of 224 FTEs, mandatory overtime, single-officer pod staffing, mental health screening rates near 70%, officer wellness, and commissioner visits to the jail.

agenda_items.title: Office of Emergency Services (OES) FY26 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brenson and OES Director Mark Lockhart presented OES highlights and FY26 budget requests, covering ambulance deliveries with 30-to-36-month lead times, relocating the Stone Park Court fleet facility by December 1 due to railroad relocation, TDMA portable radio upgrades ahead of the July 1 deadline, and an estimated $2.3 million revenue pipeline backlog caused by North Carolina's Medicaid Tailored Plan billing transition. Recommended budget items included a senior auto mechanic via relief position realignment, an emergency management deputy chief, 12 FTEs (6 EMTs and 6 paramedics) to staff one new 24-hour transport unit, five replacement ambulances, and four replacement SUVs, alongside data showing a 24.7% call volume increase since FY18 and average emergent response times hovering near 8 minutes (90th percentile around 13 minutes). Commissioners questioned staff on public safety recruitment and pay competitiveness against Wake County, community paramedicine, and integrating EMS and first responder infrastructure impacts into Planning Department development reviews.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Youth Home FY26 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Angela Nunn began the Durham County Youth Home presentation, reporting that the facility successfully opened two pods totaling 24 beds after transitioning 14 residents in 2024 and plans to open two additional pods later as staffing expands. She also highlighted that the new Youth Home achieved LEED Platinum certification in April 2025 for its energy, water, and indoor environmental performance before the video recording concluded.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session May 22th, 2025
disagreements.issue: Budgeting and Capacity Expansion for HEART Co-Response Pilot
disagreements.summary: Commissioners expressed differing emphases on whether to include resource allocations for a Sheriff's Office HEART co-response expansion pilot in the current budget cycle versus waiting for data analysis and context from the City of Durham's pilot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Include resourcing requirements in the budget if a HEART expansion pilot is a department priority
side_a_arguments: Running any pilot or trial of HEART expansion in the county will require identifiable resourcing.
Waiting through repeated planning meetings without seeing resource needs reflected in the budget delays action and makes outcome evaluation harder next year.
disagreements.side_b_position: Exercise caution on expanding capacity until data analysis, RFP findings, and City pilot context are reviewed
side_b_arguments: When the City of Durham conducted its HEART pilot, it did not expand capacity.
Understanding what the City's pilot actually required in resourcing should inform what Durham County commits to once the data analysis and RFP work are completed.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the work session; county staff indicated they would return to the board with HEART evaluation analytics and either realign existing positions or request a mid-year adjustment if needed.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session May 20th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a budget work session on May 20, 2025, led by Chair Nida Allam. Budget Director Keith Lane and County Manager Claudia Hager presented overview slides on the five-year revenue and expenditure trends, noting slowing sales tax growth, decreasing occupancy tax revenue due to state law changes, rising employee benefit costs, and funding pressures for Durham Public Schools and debt service on 2022 general obligation bonds. The manager's recommended budget proposes a 3.5-cent property tax rate increase (2.5 cents for the general fund and 1 cent for capital/debt service) to bridge a $40+ million gap between new revenue and requested expenditures.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Budget Overview & Revenue/Expenditure Trends
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane presented the FY 2025-26 budget overview, highlighting the general fund structure, slowing revenues (specifically sales tax and occupancy tax losses), increasing expenditures such as DPS funding and employee benefits, and the manager's recommended 3.5-cent property tax rate increase. Commissioners discussed the economic impacts, revaluation effects, and the use of fund balance reserves.

agenda_items.title: Financial Highlights, Audit Services RFP, & Financial Policies Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim CFO Chrystal Wright presented financial highlights including the implementation of the Gravity software for financial reporting, RFP updates for audit services and operational assessments, and the maintenance of Durham County's AAA bond rating. Commissioners discussed fund balance policies and future financial planning.

agenda_items.title: Employee Benefits Program, Leave Options, & Benchmarking Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the employee benefits program, health risk assessments, benchmarking data against peer NC counties, leave options (including paid parental leave, family leave, volunteer leave, and personal leave), and wellness initiatives. Commissioners discussed trade-offs between tax increases and employee benefit costs.

agenda_items.title: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Modernization Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief IS&T Officer Greg Mero presented an update on the county's Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) initiative to modernize and replace the 20-year-old core financial, human resources, and procurement system.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session May 12th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a regular session on May 12, 2025, featuring ceremonial proclamations for EMS Week, Memorial Day, and honoring late EMS Lieutenant Kevin M. O'Connor. The board held public hearings and approved three major unified development ordinance (UDO) text amendments and zoning items: a text amendment allowing tree coverage adjustments within development agreements (passed 3-2), a commercial general rezoning with a textual development plan for East Club at I-85 (approved unanimously), and text amendments for the Page Miami Design District (approved unanimously). They also extended the meeting to 11:30 PM before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Emergency Medical Services Week 2025
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a ceremonial proclamation recognizing May 18-24, 2025 as Emergency Medical Services Week and celebrating the 50th anniversary of Durham County EMS. Deputy Chief of Operations Gordon Smith and commissioners spoke about the vital role and dedication of EMS personnel.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Agenda Adoption & Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened the regular session, adopted the public charge and land acknowledgment, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The Board approved the meeting agenda by a 5-0 vote. Clerk Wallace presented county announcements, followed by board member remarks highlighting the Renegade Apartments public-private partnership and the Register of Deeds office.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 5-0 (Motion: Commissioner Burton, Second: Commissioner Valentine)

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Memorial Day 2025
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a proclamation declaring May 26, 2025 as Memorial Day in Durham County, honoring the 375 known soldiers, sailors, marines, airmen, and air women of Durham County who made the ultimate sacrifice. Interim Director of Veteran Services Lindseay Atkins and staff shared details on upcoming remembrance events.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring the Life and Career of EMS Lieutenant Kevin M. O'Connor
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adopted a resolution honoring the life, career, and 25 years of service of Durham County EMS Lieutenant Kevin M. O'Connor, who passed away on April 28, 2025. Commissioners and family members reflected on his dedicated service and community impact.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Tree Coverage Adjustments in Development Agreements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board held a public hearing on a privately initiated UDO text amendment to allow adjustments to tree protection and tree coverage standards via statutory development agreements. Public commenters and commissioners discussed environmental impacts, water quality, and affordable housing trade-offs.

agenda_items.title: East Club at I-85 Rezoning & Textual Development Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board held a public hearing on rezoning 13.96 acres from Residential Rural (RR) and Commercial Neighborhood (CN) to Commercial General with a textual development plan (Z240032 East Club at I-85), featuring numerous prohibited uses and tree preservation commitments.

agenda_items.title: Page Miami Design District Text Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered a text amendment for the Page Miami Design District project. Following staff presentation and board discussion, the Board approved the ordinance and consistency statement.

votes.item_title: Adopt Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: The Board of County Commissioners convened its regular session for Monday, May 12th, 2025, featuring budget presentations by Budget Director Keith Lane. Following the public charge, land acknowledgment, and pledge of allegiance led by commissioners, Clerk Wallace delivered announcements regarding the new Durham Transit Tracker dashboard, upcoming Family Fun Day 2025, and temporary closures of the Redwood Convenience Site. With no agenda adjustments proposed, the board unanimously adopted the agenda on a 5-0 vote following a motion by Commissioner Burton and second by Commissioner Valentine.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Tree Coverage Adjustments in Development Agreements (Ordinance)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Jacobs moved to adopt an ordinance amending the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) incorporating revisions to Article 3 applications and permits concerning tree coverage adjustments in development agreements, seconded by Commissioner Burton. The discussion centered on case-by-case development agreements—particularly associated with low-income housing tax credit (LITC) projects such as a triangular affordable housing site at Chin Page Road and Paige Road—and whether such agreements represent a broader trend in county zoning. Commissioners debated the applicability and staff resources required for these specialized development agreements. Ultimately, the ordinance passed by a 3-2 vote, with opposing votes cast by Stephen J. Valentine and Dr. Stelfanie Lee.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Tree Coverage Adjustments in Development Agreements (Consistency Statement)
votes.discussion_detail: As required by North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605, Commissioner Jacobs moved to adopt the accompanying consistency statement for the UDO text amendment regarding tree coverage adjustments in development agreements, seconded by Commissioner Burton. The motion followed the board's prior debate regarding development agreements and affordable housing projects on constrained parcels like the Chin Page Road and Paige Road site. Commissioners evaluated consistency with local plans and statutory standards before voting. The consistency statement passed by a 3-2 vote, with Stephen J. Valentine and Dr. Stelfanie Lee voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: East Club at I-85 Rezoning & Textual Development Plan (Ordinance)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Jacobs moved to adopt an ordinance amending the UDO incorporating revisions to Article 11 sign standards and Article 16 design districts for the East Club at I-85 rezoning request, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee. The application requested a county rezoning of 13.96 acres from residential, rural, and commercial neighborhood to commercial general with a textual development plan, receiving a unanimous recommendation of approval from the planning commission. Commissioners acknowledged planning staff's adaptation to recent state legislation and landowner outreach for this transit-oriented area site. Following discussion regarding access points, utilities, and first responder fiscal impacts, the ordinance passed unanimously (5-0).

votes.item_title: East Club at I-85 Rezoning (Consistency Statement)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Burton moved to adopt the required consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605 for the East Club at I-85 rezoning request, seconded by Commissioner Jacobs. The 13.96-acre rezoning from residential, rural, and commercial neighborhood to commercial general with a textual development plan was previously reviewed as a transit-oriented area project. Commissioners discussed the planning staff's work amidst changing state legislation and raised administrative questions regarding how future rezonings assess fiscal impacts on first responders like EMS, fire, and sheriff's deputies. The consistency statement was approved unanimously (5-0).

votes.item_title: Page Miami Design District Text Amendment (Ordinance)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a motion to adopt an ordinance amending the Unified Development Ordinance incorporating revisions to Article 11 science standards and Article 16 design districts. During discussion, commissioners and staff addressed site utilities, noting that the property utilizes a septic system without requesting city annexation or expanding sewer lines. The applicant agreed to prohibit drive-thru facilities and gas sales as an oversight correction to ensure low-intensity uses. Following the vote, commissioners raised questions regarding the lack of fiscal impact analyses for first responders (EMS, fire, and sheriff's deputies) during rezonings, to which planning staff member Sarah Young explained that developing a rezoning fiscal impact process is an ongoing implementation action from the comprehensive plan. The motion passed unanimously (5-0).

votes.item_title: Page Miami Design District Text Amendment (Consistency Statement)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a motion to adopt the required statutory consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605 for the Page Miami Design District Text Amendment. The motion was moved by Commissioner Stephen J. Valentine and seconded by Commissioner Nia Burton. The measure passed unanimously in a 5-0 vote.

disagreements.summary: Commissioners debated whether allowing tree coverage adjustments in development agreements provides vital flexibility for affordable housing or undermines environmental protections and tree canopy retention.
side_a_arguments: Necessary flexibility to support affordable housing (specifically Low-Income Housing Tax Credit projects on tight sites where parking and tree save requirements conflict) and maintain consistency with city approvals and joint planning policies.
side_b_arguments: Concerns over loss of tree canopy, exacerbating the construction sediment crisis in Southeast Durham, stormwater runoff, setting a poor precedent, and bypassing UDO tree protection standards.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: County Manager Claudia Hager FY 2025-26 Recommended Budget Presentation
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: Presenting her first recommended budget as County Manager, Claudia Hager proposed a $1+ billion total budget ($688M+ General Fund) closing a $55M+ request gap with a 3.5-cent property tax increase above the post-reappraisal revenue-neutral rate, $10.3M in new DPS current expense funding plus $10M one-time CIP funds, 11 net new FTEs, and utility/stormwater fee increases.

member_positions.stance_summary: Chair Allam thanked Manager Hager and county staff at the conclusion of the FY 2025-26 recommended budget presentation without immediate debate, deferring board questions and adjustments to the upcoming budget work sessions.
member_positions.key_quote: Thank you so much, Manager Hager, and thank you so much to all of our county staff who keep Durham County government running every single day.

bocc_manager_events.event_title: First-Responder Fiscal Impact Analysis Request Linked to Manager's Budget
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: In her FY 2025-26 budget presented earlier in the meeting, Manager Hager highlighted growing public safety demands requiring 12 new EMS positions, 5 ambulances, and 5 realigned Sheriff deputies; planning staff noted fiscal impact analyses were currently conducted only for annexations while an EMS cost methodology was under development.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs explicitly connected the East Club/I-85 rezoning staff report to the Manager's budget presented earlier that evening, pressing staff on why rezoning reports lack fiscal impact assessments for EMS, fire, and Sheriff's deputies. She urged staff to establish a methodology to capture the downstream public-safety service and equipment costs of new development.
member_positions.key_quote: I noticed there's no section about the cost or impact on first responders, and thinking about the manager's budget tonight, how can we start assessing things like the impact on EMS, on fire, on the sheriff's deputies when we have rezonings because obviously it does end up costing us more money for services and equipment.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session May 5th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a work session on May 5, 2025, discussing presentations from Urban Ministries of Durham on housing and homeless services, an update and expansion discussion on the HART co-response crisis program, and the feasibility study for the Durham County Farm Campus. The board also addressed public comments regarding school air conditioning and public safety, commissioner directives, and a substantive debate regarding a proposal to name a county facility in honor of former Mayor/Commissioner Bill Bell.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Resident Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the Durham County Board of Commissioners work session, followed by the public charge read by the Chair and a land acknowledgement read by Commissioner Burton. Resident comments included speakers addressing youth violence prevention and investment in boys/young men of color, public school air conditioning issues and capital budget allocations, and the expansion of the HEART co-responder program into the county.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Hager presented the consent agenda items, which included various grants, contracts, and programmatic approvals. Commissioners raised questions regarding specific items such as the Orange Factory Road Nature Preserve contract, the Page Miami Design District zoning map/text amendment, the EOC radio tower design contract, Go Triangle's transit assistance program (TAP), detention center repairs, and ARPA transfers.

agenda_items.title: Presentation from Urban Ministries of Durham on Operations and Collaborative Impact Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheldon Mitchell, executive director of Urban Ministries of Durham, along with project partners, presented an operational update and a proposed collaborative impact project. The presentation highlighted emergency shelter operations, housing and employment barrier reduction, and collaborative solutions to homelessness aligned with the County's DC Forward plan. Commissioners discussed partnership opportunities, supportive housing, and wrap-around services.

agenda_items.title: HEART (Holistic Empathetic Assistance Response Teams) Program Update and Expansion Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ryan Smith and the HEART team presented an operational update on the Holistic Empathetic Assistance Response Teams (HEART) program, detailing call volumes, co-response metrics, community outcomes, and external evaluations by RTI and Duke's Cook Center. Commissioners discussed potential countywide expansion, integration with 911 dispatch and the Sheriff's Office, and rural call dynamics.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Farm Campus Final Feasibility Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the final feasibility study for the Durham County Farm Campus (129-acre site in North Durham), outlining site selection, design development, community engagement across 60+ focus groups, operating budgets, and a 10-year phased implementation plan for agricultural incubation, education, and community amenities. Commissioners discussed transit access, staffing ratios, and operational funding models.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Plan FY 2026 Work Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the Durham County Transit Plan FY 2026 Work Program recommendations, budget updates, sales tax revenue projections, transit tracker launch, and capital project schedules. Commissioners discussed budget revisions, bus service expansions, microtransit, and financial oversight.

votes.item_title: Move into Closed Session
votes.mover: Not explicitly named in transcript text
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered transit-related updates, including the FY26 work program, budget adjustments such as GoTriangle's consolidated tax district administration staff resulting in a net savings of $23,000, and Durham County's increased administration project budget of $29,000 to serve as lead agency for public engagement. Presentations also highlighted safe driving milestones for GoDurham bus operators, including Tanya Burnett's recognition for two million safe miles over a quarter century of service. Additionally, updates were provided on Durham's first bus rapid transit project connecting East Durham to the Duke VA hospital campus under the regional fast 2.0 study.

disagreements.issue: Proposal to name a building or facility after former Mayor and Commissioner William V. 'Bill' Bell
disagreements.summary: Discussion regarding whether to name a county building or lobby in honor of Bill Bell, balancing his historic contributions against existing county naming policies and coordination across local government bodies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Strong support for naming a county building or prominent space in honor of Bill Bell to recognize his extraordinary lifetime of service.
side_a_arguments: Bill Bell was a transformational leader who shaped modern Durham through the city-county school merger and decades of public service.
As Durham evolves and new residents arrive, collective memory fades without prominent physical landmarks.
disagreements.side_b_position: Cautious stance supporting recognition via a lobby plaque/portrait while expressing hesitation toward naming entire buildings amidst multiple multi-agency campaigns and policy exceptions.
side_b_arguments: Concerns over multiple concurrent naming efforts and campaigns across different local governing bodies (city, county, and school board).
Importance of adhering to established county naming policies and ensuring equitable recognition of other long-serving commissioners.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken during this work session; discussion deferred for further coordination and scheduling at an upcoming meeting.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session April 28th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on April 28, 2025, opening with proclamations for Disaster Preparedness Week and the 25th anniversary of the Durham Library Foundation. The board recognized retiring Veteran Services Director Lois Harvin Raven, heard community announcements, and made board and commission appointments including to the City-County Appearance Commission. Finally, the board adjourned into a closed session for economic development negotiations before concluding the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Disaster Preparedness Week 2025

agenda_items.title: Head Start Program Funding Update & Advocacy Discussion

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session April 14th 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on April 14, 2025, chaired by Nida Alam. The board issued proclamations for Fair Housing Month, Second Chance Month, and Elizabeth Catlet Days, highlighting re-entry support and historical equity advocacy. Following discussions, the board approved the consent agenda (barring three items), and debated and voted on contracts for the new sheriff's training facility (materials testing and design/construction services), which passed 3-2. The board also authorized easement acquisitions for Slater Road, Page Park, and Chin Page Road, and approved closing the session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, Pledge of Allegiance & Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board called the meeting to order, recited the public charge, read the land acknowledgement, and recited the Pledge of Allegiance. Agenda adjustments were reviewed and approved.

agenda_items.title: Announcements & Public Notices
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Wallace read published county announcements, including budget book art submissions, Good Friday holiday office closures, the North Carolina Emergency Management Experience application, Little River Community Complex Fair, and community health promoter training.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (March 24, 2025 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the minutes for the March 24th regular session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Fair Housing Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a proclamation designating April 2025 as Fair Housing Month in Durham County. Remarks were provided by Sharon Sunk on behalf of the Durham Board of Realtors and commissioners emphasizing equitable housing access.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Second Chance Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a proclamation for Durham County Second Chance Month 2025. Justice Services Department leaders Robin Heath, Ontario Joiner, and Rashidita Royster highlighted re-entry efforts, wraparound services, and community support.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Elizabeth Catlet Days Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board honored artist and educator Elizabeth Catlet with a proclamation recognizing her history in Durham and teaching at Hillside High School. Eddie Davis and commissioners discussed her contributions and civil rights advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Black Maternal Health Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed April 11-17, 2025 as Black Maternal Health Week, discussing maternal mortality disparities, public health investments, and community-based birth support.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Line Worker Appreciation Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed April 18, 2025 as Line Worker Appreciation Day, honoring Duke Energy line workers, safety protocols, and technical training partnerships with Durham Tech.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Child Abuse Prevention Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed April 2025 as Child Abuse Prevention Month. Social Services Director Maggie Chasan and staff discussed child protective services, mandated reporting, and prevention events.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Remaining Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the consent agenda, pulling three items (Materials Testing Contract, Design/Construction Services Contract for the Sheriff's Training Facility, and MAT grant budget amendment). The remaining consent items were approved unanimously.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (Moved by Commissioner Valentine, Seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: Sheriff's Training Facility Contracts & MAT Grant Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board debated and voted on pulled consent items 25-0143 (Materials Testing Contract for New Sheriff's Training Facility) and 25-0146 (Design and Construction Services Contract for New Sheriff's Training Facility). Commissioners discussed prior votes and project opposition, ultimately passing both 3-2. Item 25-0167 (MAT grant budget amendment) was also discussed and passed 5-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 3-2 for contracts (v_bocc_2025_04_14_vainiDcmXZw_01 & 02); Passed 5-0 for MAT amendment

agenda_items.title: Easement Acquisitions for Slater Road, Page Park, and Chin Page Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board authorized the acquisition of easements for Slater Road, Page Park, and Chin Page Road, authorizing the county manager to execute purchase agreements.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (Moved by Commissioner Valentine, Seconded by Commissioner Burton)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered a closed session pursuant to NC General Statute 143-318.11(a).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (Moved by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, Seconded by Commissioner Burton)

votes.item_title: Materials Testing Contract for New Sheriff's Training Facility (25-0143)
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Dr. Lee moved and Commissioner Valentine seconded a contract with Summit Design & Engineering Services, Inc. to provide Construction Materials Testing and Special Inspections for the new Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Project No. 4310DC091) in the amount of $128,550 plus a 10% contingency of $12,855, totaling not to exceed $141,405. Project Manager Joel Jones discussed the project timeline, noting that construction was expected to span approximately 24 months following kickoff. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned aspects of the training facility project, leading to a contested debate regarding expenditures and facility planning. Dissenting members Wendy Jacobs and Michelle Burton voted NAY on the contract, expressing concerns over project scope and costs. Ultimately, the motion passed with a 3-2 vote, with affirmative votes from Vice Chair Dr. Lee, Commissioner Valentine, and Commissioner Burton.

votes.item_title: Design and Construction Services Contract for New Sheriff's Training Facility (25-0146)
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Dr. Lee moved and Commissioner Valentine seconded a design and construction services contract related to the new Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility. The board reviewed contract provisions addressing necessary architectural, design development, and construction administration services. Project details highlighted site considerations, including utility easements and vehicle accommodation adjustments required for the facility. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Burton raised specific objections and questions regarding the facility development costs and design trajectory. Dissenting members Wendy Jacobs and Michelle Burton voted NAY due to ongoing concerns with the facility's scope and budget. The motion carried 3-2, supported by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, Commissioner Valentine, and Commissioner Burton.

votes.item_title: Easement Acquisitions for Slater Road, Page Park, and Chin Page Road
votes.discussion_detail: Following a closed session discussion, Commissioner Valentine moved and Commissioner Burton seconded the authorization of necessary property easement acquisitions along Slater Road, Page Park, and Chin Page Road. The board unanimously approved the purchase agreements and authorized the County Manager to finalize negotiations to support local infrastructure development. The motion passed by a 5-0 vote with no opposition.

disagreements.side_b_position: Opposition to the sheriff's training facility

bocc_manager_events.event_title: Sheriff's Office MAT Grant Carryforward Delay & County Audit Oversight (25-0167)
bocc_manager_events.manager_position: County Manager Claudia Hager explained that the $158,000 Sheriff's Office Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) grant carryforward was a technical year-end reconciliation adjustment rather than a freeze, defending the county's centralized audit controls as consistent across all departments while acknowledging the lengthy delay was not customary and pledging to follow up.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Jacobs pulled item 25-0167 to clarify why only $6,262 of a 2023 MAT grant had been spent, but after Manager Hager and Sheriff Birkhead responded, Jacobs defended the county's public grant approval and accountability process. She clarified to Commissioner Burton that county departments must bring grants before the BOCC unlike DPS, which has its own elected school board.
member_positions.key_quote: Usually with grant funding, a lot of grants have to be approved and accepted by the board of county commissioners because it has to be a public process, we're talking about public funding and there needs to be public accountability.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Burton questioned why grant funds won by the Sheriff's Office must flow through county administration rather than going directly to the department like DPS grants. After Manager Hager defended the county's reconciliation process, Burton pushed back that the scrutiny felt like singling out the Sheriff's Office, prompting Hager to cite $30-40 million in DSS grants subject to the same single-audit rules.
member_positions.key_quote: The reason I asked that question is because I just felt like we're kind of like singling out things and I'm just trying to make sure I'm clear.

member_positions.stance_summary: Commissioner Valentine pressed Manager Hager directly on whether the multi-year bottleneck in accessing the Sheriff's Office MAT grant funds was normal county procedure. His question prompted Hager to acknowledge that the delay was not customary and commit to investigating the specific procedural breakdown.
member_positions.key_quote: I guess I was just going to ask an additional question like is it customary for that grant monies to take so long to get to where it needs to go?

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session April 7th 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its April 7, 2025 work session, opening with citizen comments on disaster preparedness, expanding the HEART program, and youth mentorship. The board proclaimed National Public Health Week, heard a comprehensive update on the Durham-Roxboro Trail feasibility study and public engagement, reviewed the economic mobility success of the Bulls life science workforce training initiative, and discussed the county naming/renaming policy regarding potential honors for former Commissioner and Mayor Bill Bell.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call & Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Lee opened the work session noting excused absences for Commissioners Jacobs and Alum. Commissioner Burton read the land acknowledgement recognizing the ancestral lands of indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens spoke on various topics including disaster preparedness committees, expanding the HEART mental health response team 24/7 and into Durham Public Schools, and youth leadership development initiatives for boys of color. Commissioners responded and thanked speakers.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Public Health Week (April 7-13, 2025)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Valentine read the proclamation designating April 7-13, 2025 as National Public Health Week with the theme 'It Starts Here'. Dr. Jenkins, Public Health Director, and board members spoke on achievements in public health and the importance of supporting public health infrastructure.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented consent items for review prior to formal regular session approval, including contracts for emergency management, Southwest Library roof replacement, lease agreements, renewable energy plan participation, and fire alarm system replacements.

agenda_items.title: Bulls Initiative / Economic Mobility Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and representatives presented updates on the Bulls Initiative, highlighting high graduation rates, life science career placements, demographics, and intergenerational economic mobility efforts in partnership with Durham Technical Community College and Durham Public Schools.

agenda_items.title: Durham Rail Trail Feasibility Study Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the feasibility study update for the Durham Rail Trail project, reviewing public survey results, community engagement workshops, trail types, planning sections from downtown to Rougemont, and next steps.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session March 24th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on March 24, 2025, featuring announcements on community events, budget portal openings, and property reappraisal appeals. The board approved the meeting agenda and presented four ceremonial proclamations recognizing Dr. John Hope and Aurelia Wedington Franklin Orchid Appreciation Day, Pearl Fryer Gardening Appreciation Day, National County Government Month, and Women in Construction. No substantive policy debates or contentious split votes occurred during this session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, Announcements & Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Netta Alam called the meeting to order, commissioner Burton delivered the land acknowledgement, and clerk Wallace read community announcements regarding upcoming events, budget portals, legal resource fairs, and youth leadership funds. The board reviewed and unanimously approved the meeting agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Britton, seconded by Commissioner Valentine)

agenda_items.title: Proclamations & Ceremonial Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented multiple ceremonial proclamations honoring John Hope and Aurelia Wedington Franklin Orchid Appreciation Day, Pearl Fryer Gardening Appreciation Day, National County Government Month (April 2025), and celebrating Women in Construction. Community speakers and staff members shared remarks highlighting local history, horticulture, county services, and workforce equity.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (March 10th Meeting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered and approved the minutes from the March 10th regular meeting without discussion or opposition.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Vice Chair Lee)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Including NCDOT 15-501 & Garrett Road Easements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed items on the consent agenda. Commissioner Valentine pulled item 25-122 regarding NCDOT easements for a grade change at the intersection of 15-501 and Garrett Road. Senior real estate officer Nancy Mitchell explained that the easements provide access roads on either side of the elevated highway as part of NCDOT's intersection improvements. Following clarification, the consent agenda was approved.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, seconded by Commissioner Valentine)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Williamson presented recommendations and appointments for various county boards and committees, including the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, City-County Appearance Commission, Women's Commission, Planning Commission, Human Relations Board, Facilities and Pollution Authority, and Library Board of Trustees. Successful applicants were congratulated.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session & Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entertained a motion to enter closed session pursuant to statutory provisions. Later in the evening, the board reconvened, noted that direction was given to staff during closed session, and adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of the Meeting Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: The meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners on March 24, 2025, opened with a public charge and land acknowledgement delivered by Commissioner Burton, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance led by Commissioner Valentine. After checking for agenda adjustments and seeing none, Commissioner Britton moved to approve the meeting agenda, which was seconded by Commissioner Valentine. The motion passed unanimously with all in favor. Following the vote, Clerk Wallace presented community announcements, including the annual women's forum, budget priority feedback portals, and upcoming legal resource fairs.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session March 10th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on March 10, 2025, discussing federal funding and policy impacts, hearing public comments on property tax revaluations, adopting several monthly proclamations (Ramadan, National Social Work Month, and Women's History Month), approving the consent agenda including capital project amendments for school general obligation bonds, and receiving a presentation on the 2024 City-County Resident Survey results.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Alam called the regular session to order, read the public charge regarding respectful behavior, and Commissioner Burton delivered the land acknowledgement recognizing indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Alam introduced an agenda adjustment to add a Ramadan proclamation. Clerk Wallace read county announcements regarding property reappraisal notices, upcoming community events, library programs, and youth budget art contests. Commissioners Jacobs and Burton also shared updates from the National Association of Counties (NACo) legislative conference.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Motion to approve agenda adjustment with Ramadan Proclamation added)

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents signed up to speak addressed the board. Victoria Peterson raised concerns regarding the distribution and transparency of federal funding (ARPA/COVID relief funds) and support for local organizations and seniors.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and considered the approval of the meeting minutes from the February 24, 2025 Regular Session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Valentine, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee)

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items & Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented several ceremonial proclamations, including a Ramadan Proclamation, a proclamation recognizing Social Work Month (featuring DSS Director Maggie Clapp), and a proclamation recognizing Women's History Month.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (ceremonial presentations and proclamations)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the consent agenda, which included capital project amendments for school obligation bonds (DSA). Commissioner Jacobs pulled items 25-01 through 25-03 for discussion regarding school capital project funding and updates.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Vice Chair Lee)

agenda_items.title: Presentation: 2024 City-County Resident Satisfaction Survey
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and representatives presented the results of the 10th consecutive City-County Resident Satisfaction Survey, detailing community feedback on county services, safety, schools, and quality of life. Commissioners discussed survey findings and community engagement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (presentation and discussion only)

agenda_items.title: Board Closing Comments and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners made closing remarks regarding the upcoming budget cycle. Commissioner Jacobs and Chair Alam requested excused absences for upcoming meetings (March 24 regular session and April 7 work session), which were approved by the board.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Excused absences approved for Commissioner Jacobs and Chair Alam)

votes.item_title: Agenda Adjustment (Add Ramadan Proclamation)
votes.discussion_detail: During the opening of the regular session, the chair requested an agenda adjustment to add a proclamation recognizing Ramadan 2025, which had been emailed to the clerk prior to the meeting. The board members indicated their approval without opposition, and the motion to approve the agenda as amended passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 24, 2025 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the approval of the meeting minutes from the February 24, 2025 regular session. Commissioner Valentine moved to approve the minutes, with a second provided by Vice Chair Dr. Lee. The minutes were approved unanimously by the board without any opposition.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Commissioner Jacobs
votes.discussion_detail: Toward the end of the meeting, Commissioner Jacobs requested an excused absence for the upcoming March 24th regular session and April 7th work session. The motion for approval was moved and seconded, and all members present voted in favor. The motion passed unanimously without opposition.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Chair Nida Alam
votes.discussion_detail: During the discussion on meeting absences, Chair Nida Alam noted that she would also need to request an excused absence for the April 7th session. A motion to approve her absence was seconded by Commissioner Valentine and passed unanimously. Vice Chair Lee confirmed she would lead the meeting on that date.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2025-02-21 10:00 AM - Annual Board Retreat
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 21, 2025 Board of County Commissioners Annual Board Retreat, County Manager Claudia Hager and Interim CFO Christily Wright led commissioners through FY 2025-26 budget planning, strategic plan alignment, and financial highlights, noting that departmental budget requests were due that day and upcoming work sessions would address capital planning, employee benefits, and public safety turnover. Wright reported that Durham County's General Fund balance reached $277 million and all-funds reserves rose from $196 million in 2014 to $444 million in 2024 (up from $419 million the prior year), compared Durham against Forsyth, Guilford, Mecklenburg, and Wake counties, and scheduled a fund balance policy discussion for April. During the board priority-setting discussion, commissioners emphasized community outreach and expressed broad alignment around program measurement, maternal and early childhood investments (including Durham Pre-K, Durham Public Schools, Durham Tech, and the BULLS Initiative), and Commissioner Stephen Valentine's focus on public safety, economic development, and reducing Durham County's 677-day median DSS child-welfare reunification time. Hager committed to compiling a priority summary ahead of March public budget input sessions and April budget updates, and the retreat adjourned without any formal motions, votes, or split disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Opening Logistics, FY 2025-26 Budget Process, and Strategic Plan Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff coordinated virtual meeting logistics before County Manager Claudia Hager opened the FY 2025-26 budget retreat, outlining morning financial reviews, afternoon economic and human-services updates from Public Health and DSS, and board priority setting. Hager explained how prior board commitments since 2018 were mapped into refined strategic plan focus areas and noted that departmental budget requests were due the same day. She previewed upcoming board work sessions covering capital planning, employee benefits, and market competitiveness in public safety.

agenda_items.title: Financial Highlights, Fund Balance Reserves, and Peer County Comparisons
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim CFO Christily Wright presented financial highlights, emphasizing prudent fund balance management amid economic uncertainty and announcing an April policy discussion with Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane. She traced reserve growth from 2014 to 2024, noting General Fund reserves reached $277 million and all-funds reserves grew from $196 million to $444 million (up from $419 million the previous year). Wright also reviewed 2024 peer comparisons of revenues, expenditures, and fund balances against Forsyth, Guilford, Mecklenburg, and Wake counties.

agenda_items.title: Community Outreach and Commissioner FY 2025-26 Budget Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff discussed resuming pre-COVID community budget outreach by partnering with local groups including the People's Alliance, the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People, and Friends of Durham. In priority presentations, commissioners highlighted performance measurement to evaluate program effectiveness, closing youth opportunity gaps, and continuing upstream investments in maternal health, early childhood, Durham Pre-K, Durham Public Schools, Durham Tech, and the BULLS Initiative. Commissioner Stephen Valentine outlined five priorities including public safety as a driver of economic development and addressing Durham County's ranking as second-lowest in North Carolina for family reunification with a 677-day median.

agenda_items.title: Retreat Wrap-Up, Public Input Calendar, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Hager noted strong alignment across commissioners' priorities despite a challenging fiscal landscape and committed to compiling a summary document and returning in April with budget highlights. She thanked the budget team, noted March public input sessions and upcoming community and PAC meetings following a weather-canceled town hall, and invited newer commissioners to reach out with questions. Commissioners thanked staff and concluded the retreat 10 minutes early without formal votes.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session Feb 3rd, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its Work Session on February 3, 2025. The board heard public comments regarding Black History Month, public records, and the foster care/family policing system. During the consent agenda review, commissioners discussed details regarding the youth home subsidy rates, open space matching grants, and property management agreements. The board voted to suspend the rules and delegate authority to the county attorney to execute a contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher risk management company. Finally, the board received major presentations on the Durham Convention Center and headquarter hotel market and financial feasibility study, the FY 2026 Transit Work Program, and the County food security initiatives implementation update.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Land Acknowledgment, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Lee called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and Commissioner Burton read the land acknowledgement. The board held a moment of silence in honor of Captain Rebecca Lobach and other victims of a tragic helicopter collision.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three public speakers addressed the board: James Chavis invited the county manager to a townhouse meeting on Black History Month and county budget; Rafi Zadi requested public records regarding carbon monoxide investigations at the DSS facility; and Amanda Wallace raised concerns regarding children in the family policing system and Durham DSS.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy manager Maurice Gough presented consent agenda items, including battery purchase contracts, health budget amendments for the 2026 community health assessment, youth home MOAs, IT disaster recovery contracts, utility agreements, lease amendments for China Walk, open space matching grants, and property management agreements. Commissioners asked questions regarding youth home per diem costs, open space grants, and retail property leasing.

agenda_items.title: County Food Security Initiatives Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County food security coordinator Reena Goldstein-Bug and Donna Rewalt presented an implementation update on county food security initiatives, reviewing food security definitions, rates, arpa-related food security projects, and future plans.

agenda_items.title: Gallagher Risk Management Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request to renew the annual insurance brokerage and risk management consulting contract with Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services. The board discussed the importance of protecting immunities while maintaining proper insurance coverage.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Suspension of rules passed unanimously; delegation of authority passed unanimously)

agenda_items.title: Durham County Convention Center and Headquarter Hotel Feasibility Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Gina propes (City of Durham) and Sean Gerson (Hunden Partners) presented the findings of the Durham Convention Center and Headquarter Hotel market and financial feasibility study. The study highlighted economic impacts of over $5 billion in net new spending over 30 years and 1,100 jobs per year. Commissioners discussed hotel capacity, walkability, community inclusion, and funding strategies.

agenda_items.title: Review of County Commissioner Directives & Meeting Wrap-up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of staff Trap reviewed board directives and received new suggestions from commissioners regarding mapping housing growth alongside service capacity (EMS, fire, sheriff, schools) and updating the agenda format to include commissioner comments.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026 Transit Work Program Presentation & Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and city transportation representatives presented the FY 2026 Transit Work Program draft, covering goDurham and goTriangle updates, brt plans, bus stop improvements, and budget allocations. Commissioners raised significant concerns regarding cost increases, increased allocation to operations & maintenance vs going more places, project delivery transparency, and accountability metrics.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Draft work program release previously approved 3-1 with Durham County voting against

agenda_items.title: RISE Assessment Center at the Youth Home Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Angela Mckinney and Jennifer McCant presented an update on the Resources for Youth Success and Empowerment (RISE) Assessment Center at the youth home, detailing walk-in/appointment services, diversion programs, upcoming summer 2025 comprehensive rollout using the CANS assessment tool, and extended operational hours.

votes.item_title: Suspend rules for Gallagher risk management contract amendment
votes.mover: Vice Chair Dr. Nida Allam (or Dr. Lee)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a procedural motion to suspend the rules regarding a contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC through January 9, 2026, in the amount of $42,000 for insurance brokerage and risk management services. Staff noted that the renewal rate and proposal remained the same as the previous year, maintaining proper immunities and insurance coverage. The motion to suspend the rules was moved by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, seconded by Commissioner Valentine, and passed unanimously with no opposition.

votes.item_title: Delegate authority to county attorney to execute contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher risk management company
votes.seconder: Vice Chair Dr. Nida Allam (Dr. Lee)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the suspension of rules, the Board considered delegating authority to the county attorney to execute the contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC through January 9, 2026, in the amount of $42,000. Staff explained that the agreement continues the previous year's terms and rates to properly navigate immunities and ensure adequate coverage. The motion was moved by Commissioner Jacobs, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, and approved unanimously by the Board.

disagreements.issue: Concerns over the FY 2026 Transit Work Program allocations, increasing operations & maintenance share vs going more places, and reporting/accountability metrics.
disagreements.summary: Debate over transit plan priorities, funding transparency, and accountability between commissioners and transit staff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Opposed to draft transit allocations and lack of delivery metrics without accountability
side_a_arguments: Commissioners expressed strong concerns that the draft FY 2026 transit work plan shifts 50% away from expanding service ("going more places") toward operations and maintenance, lacks clear project delivery metrics and accountability, and relies heavily on county funds/transit tax without adequate city skin in the game.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defending the draft plan structure while acknowledging need for refined schedules and reporting tools
side_b_arguments: Staff explained that the schedule reflects ongoing commitments, interlocal agreements involve a complex multi-agency process, and a Transit Tracker website is in development to improve reporting.
disagreements.resolution: Discussion only; items presented for information/review ahead of April decisions.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items & Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented ceremonial proclamations recognizing the 60th anniversary of the Durham Soil and Water Conservation District and celebrating the life and legacy of political titan Dr. E. Leonia Allison.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (including Capital Project Amendment for State Lottery Funds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved the consent agenda, which included items such as the Capital Project Amendment for State Lottery Funds. Board members discussed specific items before approval.
