meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session Jan 13th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on January 13, 2025, adopting the agenda, minutes, and a resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. The board debated and approved two pulled consent items: $16.5 million in limited obligation bond funding for the Sheriff's training facility (Item 24-0645, passed 3-2 after extensive debate on accountability and 911 dispatch duplication) and a preconstruction services contract for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center (Item 24-0789, passed unanimously).

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting was called to order with the reading of the public charge and indigenous land acknowledgement, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance and approval of the agenda. Clerk Wallace then presented extensive community announcements including the upcoming DC Thrive guaranteed income launch, MLK Day celebrations, food security grants, and planning department office hours.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (approval of agenda passed unanimously)

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read and formally adopted a resolution honoring the life, legacy, and impact of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., highlighting his civil rights advocacy in Durham and recommitting the county to racial equity, affordable housing, living wages, and humane labor conditions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the consent agenda excluding items pulled for separate discussion: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 for the Sheriff's Training Facility and the contract for preconstruction services for the new Emergency Operations Center / backup 911 call center.

agenda_items.title: Contract for Preconstruction Services for New Durham County EOC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed Item 24-0789 regarding preconstruction services for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and backup 911 call center. Commissioners raised questions about potential service duplication with the existing Joint City-County Durham Emergency Communications Center (DECC) and the additional $4.5 million cost for a separate sheriff's backup call center, while staff noted design flexibility moving forward.

agenda_items.title: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 - Sheriff's Training Facility \$16.5M LOB Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board engaged in extensive deliberation on Capital Project Amendment No. 25 (CPA 2022) allocating $16.5 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (LOBs) for the Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Item 24-0645). Public commenters and Commissioner Jacobs raised concerns regarding accountability, transparency, jail conditions, and demands for expanding the HEART mental health crisis response program into the county rather than funding separate facilities. Proponents emphasized staff mandates, deputy training needs, and public safety across all neighborhoods.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 3-2 (Commissioners Alam, Valentine, and Burton voting Aye; Commissioners Jacobs and Lee voting No)

agenda_items.title: Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the conclusion of agenda business and votes, the board entertained a motion for adjournment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (motion to adjourn passed unanimously)

votes.item_title: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 (CPA 2022) - $16.5M LOB funding for Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Item 24-0645)
votes.notes: Approved after extensive public comment and board debate regarding accountability, 911 dispatch duplication, and HEART expansion.
votes.discussion_detail: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 (CPA 2022) proposed appropriating $16.5 million in LOB funding for the Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Item 24-0645). Commissioners discussed accountability and transparency expectations surrounding the Sheriff's Office, referencing prior recommendations from the community safety and wellness task force. Commissioner Valentine emphasized treating the constitutional sheriff as a professional partner in governance while focusing strictly on role and function. Commissioners Nida Allam and Wendy Jacobs voted in opposition due to community concerns regarding accountability and transparency, whereas Dr. Lee moved approval and Nzinga A. Valentine seconded. The motion ultimately passed by a 3-2 vote.

votes.item_title: Contract for Preconstruction Services for New Durham County EOC (Item 24-0789)
votes.notes: Authorized county manager to execute contract for preconstruction services for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center.
votes.discussion_detail: Item 24-0789 authorized the county manager to execute a contract with the team for preconstruction services for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center (EOC). Vice chair Dr. Lee moved approval of the item, which was seconded by commissioner Valentine. Following discussion on previous matters, the board called for a vote with all members in favor and none opposed. The contract authorization passed unanimously.

disagreements.issue: Funding for Durham County Sheriff's training facility ($16.5M Limited Obligation Bonds) versus demands for accountability, transparency, 911 call center consolidation, and HEART mental health crisis response expansion.
disagreements.summary: Debate over $16.5M LOB funding for the Sheriff's training facility, balancing law enforcement training needs and statutory funding against community demands for accountability, 911 consolidation, and HEART expansion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Opposed funding the Sheriff's training facility until accountability and service integration issues are addressed.
side_a_arguments: Concerns over lack of accountability and responsiveness from the Sheriff's office, duplicative 911/backup center costs ($4.5M for separate sheriff backup vs consolidated DECC), and need for full countywide expansion of the HEART program.
disagreements.side_b_position: Supported funding the Sheriff's training facility as a vital capital improvement project.
side_b_arguments: Training facility is a necessary state-mandated capital improvement for law enforcement, provides safe and proper training, addresses community safety concerns regarding gun violence, and respects the Sheriff as an elected constitutional officer.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-2 with Commissioners Lee, Valentine, and Burton voting aye, and Chair Allam and Commissioner Jacobs voting nay.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session Jan 6th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its Work Session on January 6, 2025, presided over by Chair Nida Allam. The board heard extensive public comments concerning public safety, funding for the Sheriff's Office training facility, and the HEART unarmed crisis response program. Staff presented updates on the upcoming property tax revaluation (schedule of values, tax relief programs, and commercial/residential property trends) and a review of the Sheriff's Office training facility project and budget. No formal roll call votes or motions were recorded during this work session, as business items were previewed for upcoming regular meetings.

agenda_items.title: Meeting Opening, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Alam called the Durham County Board of Commissioners work session to order for January 6, 2025. Commissioner Burton read the public charge regarding respectful conduct, followed by a land acknowledgement recognizing indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Numerous residents and community advocates spoke during citizen comments. Major topics included urging the board not to fund the $16 million Sheriff's training facility expansion, advocating for the expansion of the HEART program countywide, expressing concerns over detention center conditions and medical costs, and discussing community engagement surrounding the firing range.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and discussed various consent agenda items, including detention center healthcare overages, interlocal agreements, library grants, the Alliance Health contract for mental health and substance use services, and the capital project amendment for the Sheriff's training facility. Commissioners asked clarifying questions regarding medical cost drivers and consent agenda procedures.

agenda_items.title: Updated Presentation on the Sheriff's Training Facility Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County engineering staff, the Sheriff's Office planning director, and architects presented an updated overview of the Durham County Sheriff's training facility project and guaranteed maximum price contract. Staff reviewed site history on a former landfill, environmental assessments, lead capture systems, firing range modernization, secure impound storage, and classroom spaces for recruit and inservice training.

agenda_items.title: Presentation on 2025 Property Revaluation and Tax Relief Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administration staff presented an update on the 2025 property revaluation process, commercial and residential market trends, upcoming public informational meeting dates, and state property tax relief programs along with Durham's low-income homeowner relief program. Commissioners discussed homeowner tax burden, statutory income limits for elderly/disabled exemptions, and revenue-neutral tax rate mechanics.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-12-10 9:00 AM - Joint City/County Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 10, 2024 Joint City/County Meeting presided over by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Board of County Commissioners and Durham City Council unanimously approved the June 11 and August 13, 2024 meeting minutes and adopted an amended 2025 Joint City/County meeting calendar by voice votes, with no split or contested votes taken. On a proposal by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and a scheduling adjustment requested by Commissioner Michelle Burton, the bodies agreed to invite the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education to the February 11 and August 12, 2025 joint meetings (consolidating an already-scheduled August 12 County–School Board meeting) and shift future joint meeting start times to 9:30 a.m. Officials also received a briefing on the City-County-DPS Housing Task Force, noting a tri-funded Housing Needs Assessment expected in late January or early February, and heard a $2.4 million joint FY2025–26 Homeless Services Advisory Committee (HSAC) budget request ($1.2 million each from the City and County) for emergency shelter and a day center alongside the County's $18 million Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) placeholder for unsheltered support. In closing discussion on depleted coordinated entry diversion and eviction diversion funds, Commissioner Jacobs advocated rapid non-congregate shelter solutions such as pallet homes while another official called for stronger post-assistance outcome tracking and transparency before committing additional eviction diversion dollars.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome Remarks, and Quorum Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding officer Dr. Mike Lee opened the joint session and deferred approval items until a quorum of both bodies arrived. Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton welcomed the newly seated County Commissioners and emphasized continued City–County collaboration on housing, crime prevention, and resident well-being.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Including Durham Public Schools in Joint City/County Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs proposed inviting the DPS Board of Education to two of the six scheduled 2025 Joint City/County meetings (February 11 and August 12) rather than converting all meetings or adding extra sessions, noting that budget and infrastructure planning—especially following Matthew Palmer's August presentation—require tri-body coordination. Council members agreed that incorporating the school board into existing calendar slots improves efficiency and streamlines transportation and infrastructure discussions, while another newly seated official supported shifting start times to 9:30 a.m.

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 11, 2024 and August 13, 2024 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Once quorum was confirmed at 00:09:24, the presiding chair returned to the deferred approval items and called for a motion on the June 11, 2024 and August 13, 2024 joint meeting minutes. The joint body approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Amended 2025 Joint City/County Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs proposed formally including DPS in the February 11 and August 12, 2025 meetings (avoiding a conflict with an already-approved August 12 County–Board of Education meeting), and Commissioner Michelle Burton requested a 9:30 a.m. start time to accommodate school drop-offs. After verifying with legal counsel that the calendar could be amended during adoption and noting April could be revisited in February, the joint body unanimously approved the amended 2025 schedule by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Update on City-County-DPS Housing Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A task force presenter reported that subcommittees have been meeting regularly and a full-group meeting will convene in January. The presenter also noted that the Housing Needs Assessment funded jointly by the City, County, and Chamber Foundation is expected to be released in late January or early February.

agenda_items.title: Homeless Services Advisory Committee (HSAC) Budget Request and Unsheltered Supports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, presenters outlined a forthcoming $2.4 million joint HSAC budget request ($1.2 million each from the City and County starting July 1) for emergency shelter ($900,000–$1 million) and a day center with supportive services, alongside existing County indirect supports such as a $1/year building lease with over $384,000 in FY2024 utilities and maintenance, Urban Ministries operational funding, and nearly $1.9 million in state energy assistance. Officials also discussed the County's $18 million CIP placeholder for unsheltered support, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs urging non-congregate pallet-home options and public-private partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Eviction Diversion Depletion and Outcome Accountability Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and officials reported that coordinated entry diversion funds are depleted and eviction diversion funds (currently capped at $2,000 per request against requests up to $8,000) will soon run out, noting demand grew sharply after pandemic-era funding compared to an earlier $180,000 baseline. A participating official raised concerns about whether short-term $2,000 grants only delay eviction by a few months and urged outcome tracking and taxpayer transparency alongside any future funding increases.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-12-09 6:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 9, 2024 Regular Session presided over by Chair Nida Allam with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners met in a one-hour closed session with no action taken and then unanimously approved all agenda, minutes, consent, and American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) reconciliation items by 5-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. During consent review, commissioners questioned Sheriff's Office staff on Item 24-0701—a five-year, $3.6 million contract for 243 body-worn and 193 in-vehicle cameras—confirming a four-year hardware service life and court-order requirements under state law for public footage access, before approving the full 15-item consent agenda including boards and commissions appointments effective January 1 (Item 24-0790). County Manager Claudia Hager led a celebratory briefing on ARPA budget reconciliation (Item 24-0742, Ordinance Amendment 25ARPA001) ensuring all contracts meet the U.S. Treasury's December 31, 2024 obligation deadline, alongside two related funding realignments (Items 24-0793 and 24-0795, Capital Project Amendment 25CP8028) covering an over-$22 million project and replacing $307,000+ in ARPA funds with debt service fund balance. The Board also adopted a ceremonial resolution read by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee observing January 1, 2025 as Emancipation Day and heard citizen comment from Minister Rafik Sadiq urging detention center security upgrades (Item 24-0713).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session on a motion by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Commissioner Michelle Burton. Upon returning to open session at 01:01:34, Chair Nida Allam announced that no action had been taken.

agenda_items.title: Opening Ceremonies, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Citizen Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam read the public charge, Commissioner Michelle Burton read the land acknowledgement, and Commissioner Stephen Valentine led the Pledge of Allegiance. The Board approved the agenda as amended (making board/commission appointments effective January 1), heard clerk announcements on holiday closures, the Stanford L. Warren Library reopening, and upcoming 2025 property reappraisal notices, and heard citizen comment from Minister Rafik Sadiq supporting detention center security improvements under Item 24-0713.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Observing January 1, 2025 as Emancipation Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee read Durham County's inaugural resolution observing January 1, 2025 as Emancipation Day, tracing North Carolina's tradition back to New Bern on January 1, 1865. Ms. Page of Concerned Black Americans Citizens (CBAC) thanked the Board and urged ongoing collaboration on closing the lineage wealth gap and expanding historically underutilized business (HUB) participation in county capital and procurement work.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 25 and December 2, 2024 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the November 25 and December 2, 2024 meetings. On a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Item 24-0701 Sheriff Body-Worn and In-Vehicle Cameras)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before voting on the 15-item consent agenda (which also included Item 24-0790 for board and commission appointments), commissioners asked Sheriff's Office leadership about Item 24-0701, a five-year, $3.6 million contract for 243 body-worn and 193 in-vehicle cameras. Officials confirmed the hardware meets current staffing needs (with a typical four-year Motorola service life) and stated that public release of footage requires a judge's court order under state law; the full consent agenda then passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Budget Reconciliation (24-0742) and Related Funding Realignments (24-0793, 24-0795)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager presented the ARPA reconciliation aligning all contracts ahead of the December 31, 2024 U.S. Treasury obligation deadline (with spending through December 31, 2026) and prioritizing child services subsidies and food security as contingency areas. She also explained two companion items adjusting enterprise and ARPA funds for an over-$22 million project and replacing over $307,000 in ARPA funding with debt service fund balance; the Board unanimously approved all three items in separate votes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; all five seated commissioners were confirmed present and active throughout the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Board convened in closed session for approximately one hour and reported no action taken upon returning to open session at 01:01:34.

votes.item_title: Approval of Agenda as Amended (Effective January 1 Language for Appointments)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Any opposed? Agenda is moved').
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nida Allam adjusted the boards and commissions appointments language to specify an effective date of January 1.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 25 and December 2, 2024 Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved November 25 and December 2, 2024 Board minutes without modification.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0742: ARPA Budget Reconciliation and Grant Ordinance Amendment No. 25ARPA001
votes.discussion_detail: Moves ARPA funding between functional areas to align with final project authorizations and approves contract amendments ahead of the December 31, 2024 Treasury obligation deadline.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0793: Budget Amendment Realigning Enterprise Fund and ARPA Project Allocation
votes.discussion_detail: Reduces enterprise fund allocation and increases ARPA funding for a major capital project totaling over $22 million.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0795: Capital Project Amendment No. 25CP8028 and Budget Ordinance Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Realigns funding by removing over $307,000 in ARPA funding from the project and replacing it with debt service fund balance.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-12-02 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 2, 2024 organizational meeting—opened briefly by County Attorney Larissa Williamson under North Carolina statute until the Board elected its chair—the Durham Board of County Commissioners swore in Register of Deeds Sharon A. Davis and the 2024–2028 Board cohort (Michelle Burton, Dr. Mike Lee, Stephen Valentine, Wendy Jacobs, and Nida Allam). By unanimous 5-0 roll-call/voice votes, the Board re-elected Nida Allam as Chair and elected newly seated Commissioner Dr. Mike Lee as Vice Chair, with no split or contested votes. Following inaugural remarks from the commissioners emphasizing housing affordability, mental health, food security, and public education, the Board twice voted 5-0 to suspend its rules to take immediate formal action. Under the suspended rules, the Board unanimously approved statutory public official bonds for the Sheriff, Tax Administrator, Chief Financial Officer, and Register of Deeds, and adopted its 2025 Board of County Commissioners meeting schedule.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Election Certification Note, and Oaths of Office
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Larissa Williamson presided over the statutory organizational opening, noting Elections Director Derek Bowens confirmed election certification and mailed certificates directly to candidates. Chief District Court Judge Clayton Jones administered the oath of office to Register of Deeds Sharon A. Davis, followed by the swearing-in of commissioners Michelle Burton (by Judge Shamieka Rhinehart), Dr. Mike Lee, Stephen Valentine, Wendy Jacobs, and Nida Allam (with Justice Allison Riggs also participating).

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair (Nida Allam)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Williamson called for nominations for Board Chair and conducted a roll call following Nida Allam's nomination. All five commissioners voted in favor, unanimously electing Nida Allam as Chair, who then assumed the gavel.

agenda_items.title: Election of Vice Chair (Dr. Mike Lee) and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam entertained a motion to nominate Dr. Mike Lee as Vice Chair, which passed unanimously. Commissioners delivered inaugural remarks thanking family, faith communities, and supporters while highlighting priorities around housing costs, food insecurity, mental health, substance use, and public education.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Approval of Public Official Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Curtis Massey presented the statutory public official bonds recommended by risk management and staff for the Sheriff, Tax Administrator, Chief Financial Officer, and Register of Deeds for filing with the Register of Deeds and Clerk of Court. The Board unanimously voted to suspend its rules and then unanimously approved the bonds.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Approval of 2025 BOCC Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam introduced the 2025 Board of County Commissioners meeting calendar posted in Legistar. The Board unanimously voted to suspend its rules and then unanimously adopted the 2025 meeting schedule before adjourning to a lobby reception.

votes.item_title: Election of Nida Allam as Chair of the Board of County Commissioners
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 roll-call vote; Clerk called Michelle Burton, Dr. Mike Lee, Stephen Valentine, Wendy Jacobs, and Nida Allam.
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Larissa Williamson conducted a roll-call vote of the five newly sworn-in commissioners.

votes.item_title: Election of Dr. Mike Lee as Vice Chair of the Board of County Commissioners
votes.notes: Unanimous vote (transcript omits the remaining individual roll-call responses in a gap before remarks, with all five commissioners present at the organizational ceremony).
votes.discussion_detail: Nominated without opposition; Chair Nida Allam initiated the vote starting with Commissioner Stephen Valentine.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules to Vote on Public Official Bonds
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural suspension required to act on the bonds during the organizational work session.

votes.item_title: Approval of Statutory Public Official Bonds
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote. Note: transcript ASR rendered the seconder as 'commissioner bern', referring to newly seated Commissioner Michelle Burton.
votes.discussion_detail: Approves statutorily required public official bonds procured through risk management for the Sheriff, Tax Administrator, Chief Financial Officer, and Register of Deeds.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules to Vote on 2025 Meeting Schedule
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote. Transcript ASR rendered the seconder as 'commissioner bern', referring to newly seated Commissioner Michelle Burton.
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural suspension to take action on the 2025 Board calendar during the organizational meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2025 Board of County Commissioners Meeting Schedule
votes.discussion_detail: Adopts the 2025 regular and work session meeting schedule for the Board of County Commissioners.
